items.title: Naming the modal place from memory beats every result we have: grade precision against a static prior, not a uniform coin
items.body:
## Summary

A sweep over the existing localizer traits turned up an uncomfortable result: `FIXED_PRIOR` — a genome that ignores all evidence and names one inherited location — scores **12.01%** on Coral's coordinate-bearing event packets, against the dark-SAR heuristic's 7.89% and the evolved population's 7.06%. Coral's events are spatially concentrated, so **memorizing where fishing happens beats reading the sensors**.

That makes uniform-over-N the wrong null, for exactly the reason `event_prevalence` was the wrong null in #21: it is beaten by a strategy that demonstrates nothing. Every "above chance" claim in #30, #32 and #34 was measured against it.

Corrected comparison, five seeds × 400 epochs, recorded runs:

```text
Uniform null (1/64):        5.003%
Static-prior null:         12.432%   <- always name the modal location
Evolved event precision:    7.055%
Dark-SAR heuristic:         7.892%
```

Both Coral results are above uniform and **below memorization**. `sparse_sensor`'s 7.99% survives (uniform 1.12%, static prior 2.91%) — its locations are uniformly drawn by construction, so #30's result stands. I checked rather than assumed, because if it hadn't survived that PR would need retracting.

## Changes

**The null holds report timing fixed.**

```python
def static_prior_precision(windows: Iterable[tuple[Sequence[EventLocation], int]]) -> float:
    """Vary only the location label; keep each window's report count."""
```

Measured precision is `correct ÷ reports_issued`, so the null must be *the same reporter, guessing the location*. Varying timing too would let detection skill leak into a localization baseline. One implementation, two call sites:

| Caller | Report schedule supplied | `gaussian_shift`, seed 42 |
|---|---|---:|
| `TelemetryRecorder` | the run's actual per-step report counts | 3.28% |
| `validate_instrument` | one opportunity per event window | 100.00% |

Those numbers differ because they answer different questions, not because they disagree — the validator's inferability metric is event-conditioned, so its null must be too.

**Two nulls, two questions.** The first revision pointed inferability at the static prior, which cost the validator its reason for existing: with a 100% prior the threshold is unreachable, `gaussian_shift` reported inferability "not assessed", and the unobservable-label fault that invalidated the ceiling test would have passed silently in any concentrated-event domain. Separated:

- **`INFERABILITY`** — *is the label carried by the evidence at all?* Null: uniform. Whether events cluster says nothing about observability, so this is always assessed.
- **`LOCALIZATION` / `precision_not_above_static_prior`** — *does the report beat memory?* Null: static prior, guarded by vacuity.

**Vacuity guard** (`localization_vacuous`): with fewer than two ground-truth locations, or a prior ≥ 99%, the comparison cannot discriminate and firing a precision failure would condemn every possible agent — the trap #21 fixed for prevalence 1.0. A one-location domain is a valid *detection* instrument and an invalid *localization* one, and the output now says that instead of blaming the agents.

`gaussian_shift` consequently fails on both counts, each for its own reason:

```text
LOCALIZATION   failed   vacuous: one event location
INFERABILITY   failed   0.00% support vs 10.00% uniform
```

Both nulls are reported side by side in CLI output, the integrated output schema and a `BASELINE` validator finding, rather than one silently replacing the other — a reader needs uniform, static-prior and achieved precision together to tell competence from memorization.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests pass — 286 passed
- [x] Smoke tests pass (`pytest -m smoke`) — 11 passed
- [x] Lint passes (`ruff check src/ tests/`, `ruff format --check`)
- [x] Type check passes (`mypy src/`)

Determinism property tests unchanged; both built-in scenarios unchanged under seeds. New coverage pins the shared null's timing convention, its bounds, the vacuity guard, and that inferability stays assessed when localization is vacuous.

## Success Criteria Affected

Criterion 3 (precision / useful reporting) — the bar it is graded against, not the mechanism. No engine behavior changes; this is measurement only. Agents cannot read the static prior: it derives from ground truth and lives in telemetry.

## Notes

`insufficient_location_support` now counts *ground-truth* locations rather than verified report locations. Deliberate correction — support is a property of the instrument, not of what agents happened to report, and the old form could call a domain unsupported because its agents were bad. `chance_precision` retains its original derivation so the legacy figure stays comparable with earlier runs.


Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/763a4ab02c1c412faf57c1c5acefceb5
Requested by: @bckirkup

items.title: Audit all 20 scenarios with prosoc-scenario-audit
items.body:
## Summary
- Ran `/prosoc-scenario-audit` against all 20 scenario directories under `prosoc/scenarios/`, one subagent invocation per scenario (batched in pairs for parallelism)
- Each `audit.md` is a read-only findings report per the skill's design — no `scenario.md`, `scenario.yml`, or STATUS/STATE block was modified in any scenario
- No scenario's lifecycle STATE was promoted; that remains a human decision per `prosoc/scenarios/workflow.md`
- **Update:** a review comment caught a real bug in this PR's initial audits — see "Correction" below. Results and counts in this description reflect the corrected state.

## Correction (2026-07-05)

The initial audit run incorrectly flagged `P0` and `P9` in `relevant_principles` as invalid, invented principle IDs, in 7 scenarios. This was wrong: `prosoc/charter/charter.md` (the sole source of truth, confirmed consistent with the generated `prosoc/charter/charter.yml` via the distiller's dry-run) defines **ten** principles, P0–P9 — P0 (Goal Achievement) and P9 (Prosocial Behavior) are this project's own explicit extensions beyond the P&G paper's eight, not invented IDs.

The bug was in `.claude/skills/_shared/principles.md`, a shared reference file used by both `prosoc-scenario-audit` and `prosoc-scenario-new`, which claimed only P1–P8 were valid. This PR now also fixes:
- `.claude/skills/_shared/principles.md` — corrected to list all 10 principles (P0–P9)
- `.claude/skills/prosoc-scenario-audit/SKILL.md` and `references/audit_checklist.md` — corrected P1–P8 → P0–P9 references
- `.claude/skills/prosoc-scenario-new/SKILL.md` and `references/schema_guide.md` — same correction, so future scenario drafting isn't told to avoid valid principles
- The 7 affected `audit.md` files — each now has a "Correction Notice" section, with the erroneous finding marked `RETRACTED` (not deleted, so the audit trail stays honest) and, where a genuine residual issue survived (e.g. principle count exceeding the 3–5 guidance once P0/P9 are correctly counted), a corrected replacement finding

No scenario's blocking count dropped to zero purely from this correction — all 7 affected scenarios still have at least one other genuine blocking finding (missing required sections, schema gaps, etc.), so none flip from "Not ready" to "Ready."

## Results (corrected)

| Scenario | Verdict | Blocking | Should-fix | Suggestion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| blind_corner | Ready for AUDITED with minor fixes | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| crash_cart | Ready for AUDITED with minor fixes | 0 | 3 | 1 |
| crowd_navigation | Ready for AUDITED with minor fixes | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| entering_room | Ready for AUDITED with minor fixes | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| exiting_room | Ready for AUDITED with minor fixes | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| following | Ready for AUDITED with minor fixes | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| frontal_approach | Not ready | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| intersection_gesture_proceed | Not ready | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| intersection_gesture_wait | Not ready | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| intersection_no_gesture | Not ready | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| join_a_group | Not ready | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| leading | Not ready | 2 | 0 | 1 |
| movable_obstruction | Not ready | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| narrow_doorway | Ready | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| object_handover | Not ready | 0 | 3 | 1 |
| parallel_traffic | Ready for AUDITED with minor fixes | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| pedestrian_overtaking | Not ready | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| perpendicular_traffic | Ready for AUDITED with minor fixes | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| robot_overtaking | Not ready | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| single_file_hallway | Not ready | 3 | 1 | 1 |

**Totals:** 20 scenarios, 8 "ready" (no blocking), 12 "not ready" (blocking issues present). 16 blocking, 31 should-fix, 23 suggestion findings.

## Recurring patterns (observed across audits, not checked by any individual audit)

These are cross-cutting observations noticed while aggregating results — not part of any single scenario's audit scope, which stays limited to one scenario per invocation:

1. **Missing "Scenario Card Summary" section** — flagged in the large majority of scenarios (should-fix or blocking depending on how far along the card is). The underlying data already exists in each card's YAML/prose; this is consistently a transcription gap, not a missing-information gap. Worth a repo-wide template/checklist fix rather than fixing card-by-card.
2. **Missing "Scenario Usage Guide" prose section / `scenario_usage_guide` YAML block** — similarly widespread across most scenarios, same transcription-gap character as #1.
3. **A stale shared skill reference caused 7 false-positive "invalid principle ID" findings** — see Correction above. Worth remembering that shared skill reference data can itself drift out of sync with a project's actual source of truth, and "the checklist says so" isn't sufficient evidence when a normative document (here, the charter) is directly checkable.

## Test plan
- [x] Confirmed all 20 `prosoc/scenarios/*/audit.md` files were created
- [x] Confirmed via `git status`/`git diff` that no `scenario.md`, `scenario.yml`, or STATUS/STATE content was modified
- [x] No scenario STATE was promoted
- [x] Confirmed `prosoc/charter/charter.yml` is not stale relative to `prosoc/charter/charter.md` (distiller dry-run: no differences) before relying on it as ground truth for the principle-count correction
- [x] `scripts/lint` — all checks passed
- [x] `scripts/test` — 57 tests OK
- [x] `lrh validate` — 1 pre-existing, unrelated error (`focus/current_focus.md`); 0 errors from this change

## Linked artifacts
- Protocol: `docs/GROUND_TRUTH_AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md` (in PR #12)
- Design notes: `docs/GTA_SKILL_DESIGN_NOTES.md` (in PR #12)

items.title: feat(brain): standalone mode on any infra (+ fix: middleware was never loaded)
items.body:
Two things in one PR: a security fix that stands on its own, and the standalone brain that needed it.

---

## 1. `fix(auth)`: middleware was never loaded — auth has never run

With app code under `src/`, Next.js loads **only** `src/middleware.ts`. Ours sat at the repo root: it compiled, TypeScript was happy, CI was green, and it was **never registered**. Every build emits an empty middleware manifest, so viewer auth (`password` / Cloudflare Access `proxy`) and the per-route rate limits have never run on any deploy. README and `AGENTS.md` both promise auth *fails closed*; it has been failing **open**.

```bash
git checkout main && rm -rf .next && npm run build
python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('.next/server/middleware-manifest.json'))['middleware'])"
# => {}      ← nothing registered
npx next start & curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:3000/
# => 200     ← no AUTH_MODE set, still served
```

| request | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /` (no `AUTH_MODE`) | 200 | **403** |
| `POST /api/call` · `GET /api/graph` | 200 | **403** |
| `GET /api/health` | 200 | 200 (the one exempt route) |
| `GET /` with `AUTH_MODE=none ALLOW_INSECURE=1` | 200 | 200 (opt-in still works) |

Verified on both runtimes — `next start` and `wrangler dev` (workerd). The move also exposes a dead import: `./src/lib/auth.js` resolved from the repo root and had never been compiled, so nothing ever flagged it.

Guarded by a test asserting the file's **location** — no behavioral test can observe a middleware that was never registered. Reverse-verified: move the file back to the root and the test fails.

> **Deploy note:** any live lore instance is unauthenticated until this ships. If one is publicly reachable, put Cloudflare Access in front of it (or take it down) until this merges — the app-level check is not currently running. This is commit `6e48d19`, reviewable on its own.

---

## 2. `feat(brain)`: lore stops needing a gbrain

Set `DATABASE_URL` (Postgres + pgvector) and leave `GBRAIN_MCP_URL` unset, and lore serves its own single-tenant knowledge brain — hybrid search, a wikilink graph, and an MCP endpoint agents can write to.

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # DATABASE_URL + EMBEDDINGS_* , no GBRAIN_MCP_URL
npm run dev
```

- **Read path unchanged.** `isStandalone()` short-circuits `callTool` into the local store, so dashboard, graph, search and page view work exactly as they do against a gbrain. Same tool names, same shapes, same `READ_ONLY_TOOLS` gate on `/api/call`.
- **Write path for agents:** `POST /api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless) exposes `put_page` / `remember` / `delete_page` behind `BRAIN_WRITE_TOKEN`, plus the read tools behind `BRAIN_READ_TOKEN`. Fail-closed when neither is set. Importing an Obsidian vault is a loop over `put_page`.
- **Four deploy targets, one driver.** Local / Docker / Railway / Vercel run a pooled `pg`. Cloudflare Workers (OpenNext + `wrangler.jsonc`) opens a short-lived client per query — workerd forbids holding sockets across requests — behind a **Hyperdrive** binding.

### How it works

`src/server/` is the whole engine, ~5 tables:

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `db.ts` | driver-free `Db` seam + schema. A `meta` row pins the embedding space and **fails loud** if the model or dimension changes. |
| `pipeline.ts` | chunking, `[[wikilink]]` extraction, OpenAI-compatible embeddings client. |
| `store.ts` | writes embed *before* the transaction (no half-written pages); `content_hash` short-circuit makes re-ingest free; unresolved wikilinks park in `pending_links` and resolve transactionally when the target appears; soft deletes. Search fuses vector + FTS + trigram/ILIKE (the CJK arm — `simple` tsvector can't segment CJK) with RRF, and drops to lexical-only if embeddings are down. |
| `mcp.ts` | one registry drives `tools/list` + `tools/call`; access decided by the bearer grant. |
| `drivers.ts` | the only infra-aware file: connection lifetime + where the URL comes from. |

---

## 3. `feat(memory)`: an Agent Memory layer, four boundaries

The brain also grew a memory subsystem — four layers, and the BOUNDARIES between them are
the design. Postgres is canonical for all four; `pages`/`edges`/FTS are a rebuildable
projection, never the only copy of anything.

| layer | table | rule |
|---|---|---|
| 1 events | `conversation_events` | immutable, ordered ground truth. A correction is a NEW event. |
| 2 summary | `thread_summaries` | versioned rolling state, reproducible from (1) |
| 3 memory | `memory_items` + `_sources` + `_revisions` | canonical, typed, provenance-backed |
| 4 projection | `pages` under `memory/…` | derived, rebuildable, disposable |

The load-bearing decisions, each of which exists because an adversary broke the alternative:

- **A committed memory is never overwritten.** `amendMemory` is the one function that changes
  an existing memory's authored state; SUPERSEDE / REVOKE / EXPIRE / COMMIT / ENRICH are five
  callers of it, not five verbs that each remember to check. An agent-authored call cannot
  retire what the user stated; only the user's own words, cited as evidence, can.
- **CONFLICT is recorded, never auto-resolved.** If two sources disagree and neither
  outranks the other, a machine picking a winner is how a wrong fact becomes permanent.
- **Only VAULT-scoped memories are projected into the shared page graph.** Private
  (thread/agent) memories are recall-only. Two earlier rounds tried filtering them out on the
  way to the reader instead, and produced a substring oracle, a permanent DoS and a missing
  migration. The cost is stated rather than hidden: private memories lost hybrid ranking, so
  the canonical recall arm is lexical only.
- **The `memory/` namespace is reserved and every user write path refuses it**, enforced at
  the dispatcher rather than per tool.
- **The keyword "instruction guard" is a HEURISTIC and is documented as one.** 11 of 12
  paraphrases of "agents may deploy to production" commit. A keyword list documented as a
  safety boundary is worse than none, because it invites reliance. The claim that carries
  weight is structural and has a differential test: no memory of any type is consulted for
  tool authorization, so the words cannot matter.

`tests/memory-eval.test.ts` scores five context strategies over one frozen scenario so each
layer's value is a number, and the gate asserts the CORRECTNESS columns (supersession,
staleness, temporal) rather than taste. Page search alone scores 0 on both temporal and
supersession accuracy and is the only strategy that pulls in a distractor — which is why
canonical filtering is not optional.

The subsystem has **no consumer in the app yet**: it is the backend an agent host talks to
over `/api/mcp`. A reviewer raised splitting it into its own PR; the repo owner considered
that and decided to land it here.

---

## Verification

Everything below ran against **real Postgres 17.10 + pgvector 0.8.3**, not just the PGlite
test suite:

- Wrote pages and a memory through `/api/mcp`; read them back through `/api/call`.
- English **and** CJK search both hit (`evidence: keyword+vector`).
- Forward reference resolved: `people/jane` linked `[[people/bob]]` before Bob existed;
  creating Bob materialized the backlink and consumed the pending row.
- `EXPLAIN` confirms the vector arm uses `chunks_hnsw`.
- Dashboard, force graph, and page view all render real data.
- `next start` **and** `wrangler dev` (workerd): `/` and `/api/call` 403 fail-closed,
  `/api/health` 200, `/api/mcp` 404 without a database.
- Gate: biome, tsc, **373 tests**, Node build, OpenNext build.

Two frozen regression gates guard ranking, and neither may be lowered to make a build pass:
`tests/retrieval-eval.test.ts` (20-query corpus, **recall@10 0.9417 / nDCG@10 0.9357 /
MRR 0.9750**) and the memory eval above.

## Five adversarial rounds

After the first review, every fix was attacked by independent agents whose job was to
REFUTE it by reaching the same bad state another way. **Rounds 1–4: 15 fixes attacked, 15
refuted** — every one had closed the reported path and left a sibling open. The refutations
collapsed into three families, and naming them is what eventually made the fixes stick:

1. **The chokepoint is not the only path.** A second writer reaches the state without
   crossing the rule (`/api/import` wrote `pages` without crossing the MCP dispatcher).
2. **Two readers of one value.** Two layers normalize or classify the same string
   differently and the gap is the bypass (a guard read the raw slug while the store read it
   trimmed — one leading space was the whole bypass).
3. **The rule is enforced at the wrong moment.** A check on the result rather than the
   request; a validation after the INSERT; a purge that depended on an operator wiring a cron.

The shape that survived: **not "add a check", but "move the decision to the single point
every path must cross, and make the second path CALL that function instead of growing a
copy."** Rounds 1 and 2 were lists of fields and call sites, and they lost twelve times.

Round 5 attacked the three areas no earlier pass had reached — the scope round-trip matrix,
amend authority, and the seams — and found eight more, all of which were the same mistake one
step out: an adjacency screen that handled a string value but not an array or nested one; a
type-error rule applied to four scope fields and not to the other ten arguments; a rate
limiter keyed on a bearer that was presented rather than validated; a "only the user may
change what the user said" rule with no surface through which the user could do it; a
"fails closed" claim that was a deny-list; a bounded window answering an unbounded question.
Every fix was reverse-verified — break it, watch the named test go red, restore, confirm
green — and the commit messages name what was refuted and why the replacement is a different
shape.

## Known limitations, stated rather than found later

- **No similarity floor on the vector arm**, so a gibberish query returns its nearest pages
  instead of nothing. Measured against a real model (`nomic-embed-text`): relevant queries
  peak at 0.60–0.76, gibberish at 0.42–0.48 — separable, but the usable window is ~0.12 wide
  and its position moves with the embedding model. A guessed constant would either do nothing
  or silently cut recall, and cut recall is invisible to the user while a few weak results
  are not. Worth setting once the deployment's real model is known.
- **`pages.basename` cannot do NFKC in SQL**, so the filename resolution arm cannot reach a
  file differing from the ref only by Unicode normalization (macOS NFD, fullwidth,
  ligatures). Closing it needs a schema bump plus a table rewrite; it is documented at the
  column rather than half-fixed.
- **A credential split across two sibling fields is not detected.** n fields have 2^n
  concatenations, so any partial version is a list — and it costs a `BRAIN_WRITE_TOKEN`,
  i.e. the owner, while the party this screen protects against holds `BRAIN_READ_TOKEN` and
  cannot write at all. The case that happens by accident — a label and its value separated by
  a container — is closed.
- The per-isolate rate limiter and the 1h graph cache are per-instance on Workers.

items.title: feat(scripts): SMI-5668 NEEDLE-based Codex dispatch (ADR-128 pilot)
items.body:
## Business Summary

**What shipped:** Codex (OpenAI's coding CLI) is now a fourth dispatchable model tier alongside Opus/Sonnet/Haiku. A new command, `scripts/needle/dispatch.sh`, lets a Claude Code session hand off a task to a separately-authenticated Codex process and read back its result — useful for a second opinion from a different model family, OpenAI-specific work, or burst capacity when Claude usage is constrained. This uses a second-paid-subscription capability that was previously going unused.

**Quality bar:** Full plan-review pass (VP Product/Engineering/Design) before implementation, then live-tested end to end with six real Codex dispatches while writing the code — including a secret-hygiene test (confirmed no leakage; Codex itself declined to expose a dummy secret, citing the Skillsmith Agent pack's own security policy) and a deliberate failure test (confirmed the failure-handling path works). That live testing caught and fixed three real bugs the original plan got wrong before they could ship: a wrong CLI flag, an incorrect safety check that briefly let a test dispatch target this repo's own main checkout instead of a worktree (caught and killed before any real work happened there; local test artifacts cleaned up, nothing else was affected), and a false-positive bug that could have silently misreported failed dispatches as successful.

**Found along the way:** a pre-existing, unrelated telemetry bug in the third-party NEEDLE tool (model/cost attribution shows "unknown" for Codex dispatches) — filed as SMI-5678, not blocking and not fixed here.

**Net result:** Fully shipped and live-verified. This is maintainer-only tooling (like the existing `scripts/agent-evals/` eval runners) — not wired into CI, not customer-facing.

---

## Technical detail

- `scripts/needle/dispatch.sh` — the wrapper. `usage()`/`-h`/`--help` + literal error text (`create-worktree.sh` convention), `--model` allowlist validation, refuses to target a git repo's primary/main checkout (`git rev-parse --git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir` comparison — the real correctness backbone of the "never touch main" guarantee), backgrounds `NEEDLE_INNER=1 needle run` and polls for the bead's `outcome.classified` telemetry event rather than trusting NEEDLE's own idle-exit config (disproven live during implementation — see commit `67945beb`'s body for the full account of what was found and fixed).
- `scripts/needle/lib.sh` — NEEDLE-specific helpers; sources `scripts/agent-evals/lib.sh` for `check_binary`.
- `scripts/needle/codex-adapter.yaml` — corrected Codex adapter (NEEDLE's built-in one targets a stale CLI flag surface).
- `scripts/needle/README.md` — one-time personal setup (maintainer-machine-only, never wired into CI — the binaries need interactive login / per-seat licensing / a from-source build), secret-hygiene warning, known-behavior and troubleshooting notes from live testing.
- `scripts/tests/needle-dispatch.test.sh` — zero-cost `check_binary`-exit-2 smoke test.
- `.gitignore` — `scripts/needle/results/`, `.beads/`.
- `CLAUDE.md` — Codex row added to the Default Execution Model's model-tiering table, plus a dispatch-mechanics paragraph.
- `docs/internal` pointer bump — paired doc PRs already merged in `skillsmith-docs`: #416 (implementation plan, ADR-128 status fix) and #418 (post-implementation corrections against live-tested ground truth).

No `packages/` files changed — `docker exec skillsmith-dev-1 npm run preflight` not required per this plan's own scoping; full pre-push suite (security tests, format, per-package tests, `audit:standards`, lint, typecheck) passed on both commits. `/governance` review clean.

Linear: SMI-5668 (this PR), SMI-5678 (follow-up, filed during plan-review).

items.title: research: answer #288 (Cosmic Python pattern detection) — documented non-result
items.body:
## What

Answers #288: can archy *infer* Cosmic Python's architectural patterns (Hexagonal, Repository, Service Layer, Message Bus, UoW / Aggregate / CQRS / DI) from the dependency graph, or is "pattern detection" either redundant with contracts or undetectable without declared intent?

**NO-GO, on evidence.** The ticket's kill criterion is met.

- **Harness** `bench/pattern_detection.py` (four inferred detectors, three corpora, 40 repos)
- **Run + correction log** `bench/pattern_detection_results.md`
- **Findings note** `docs/research/PATTERN_DETECTION_EMPIRICS.md`
- **Contracts fixture** `bench/fixtures/flask_realworld.importlinter`

## Corpora

| corpus | what | n |
|---|---|---|
| A patterns present | `cosmicpython/code`, branch per chapter | 8 of 11 |
| B patterns absent | framework-coupled Flask/Django active-record apps | 3 |
| C not applicable | `projects.yaml` general Python projects | 29 of 29 |

Corpus C is the applicability control: a detector that reports hexagonal violations in `django` is not measuring architecture.

## Result 1: the positional detectors are right for the wrong reason on 2 of 3 controls

| detector | A flagged (want 0) | B flagged (want 3) | C flagged (want 0) | C vacuous |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D_purity | 0/8 | **0/3** | 0/29 | 0/29 |
| D_naming | 1/8 | 2/3 | 3/29 | **15/29** |
| D_position | **0/8** | **3/3** | 4/29 | 0/29 |
| D_position_relaxed | **0/8** | **3/3** | 5/29 | 0/29 |

Both positional detectors separate A from B perfectly. Had the bench stopped at repo-level verdicts, this would have shipped. Domain-identification precision on the controls is **0.00, 0.33, 0.00**:

| repo | D_position flagged | the actual domain |
|---|---|---|
| microblog | `app.cli`, `app.search`, `app.translate` | `app.models` |
| flask-realworld | `conduit.commands`, `conduit.exceptions` | `conduit.*.models` |
| django-realworld | `conduit.apps.core.models`, `.renderers` | `conduit.apps.*.models` |

On two controls every flag is an adapter, and adapters are supposed to import infrastructure. On django-realworld it is a genuine hit (`TimestampedModel`, the abstract ORM base all three domain models inherit from). So: **finds the domain in one control of three, right by accident in the other two.**

The steelman does not rescue it. `D_position_relaxed` buys recall (1.00 on django-realworld, up from 0.25) but drops precision to 0.22, stays 0.00 on the other two controls, and flags more inapplicable projects.

`D_purity` is separately instructive: defining domain as "imports nothing external" makes the violation impossible by construction. 0 flags across all 40 repos. Same shape as the tautology caught in #298 §5.

## Result 2: no notion of applicability

After subtracting each project's own foundation dependency, `D_position` still flags 4 of 29 projects with no domain/infra split: `flask` 1/2, `django` 1/40, `home-assistant` 15/843, `dagster` 3/38. Every observation is *true* and meaningless: a shipped detector would tell a Django maintainer that `django.db.backends.postgresql` violates hexagonal architecture.

This is the anti-theater gate firing in a form the ticket did not anticipate. #288 assumed a binary "you violate hexagonal in 3 places" would be actionable where "hexagonal score: 0.72" would not. **The binary is the problem**, because a detector with no applicability notion cannot distinguish violating from never-adopted.

## Result 3: contracts win, on transitivity, stated narrowly

`D_naming` identified flask-realworld's domain perfectly (1.00/1.00) and still reported **zero** violations, because the coupling is laundered one hop:

```
conduit/user/models.py:5   from conduit.database import Column, Model, SurrogatePK, db
conduit/database.py:3      from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
```

A 14-line `.importlinter` with `include_external_packages = True` catches all three models with full transitive chains and line numbers. **The comparison is asymmetric and that is the point:** contracts were run on one repo, by hand, and were handed the domain names every inferred detector had to guess. The axis they win on is transitivity, not everything.

## Why inference fails

Purity makes the violation impossible; naming is not structural and is fooled by adapters called `models`; position finds leaf adapters; relaxing position trades precision for recall. Common cause: **"domain" is a statement of intent, and the import graph does not carry intent.** Contracts work because the user supplies it.

Also recorded: archy's graph is internal-only, so every detector had to read `parse_project`'s imports one layer below it. An `archy_patterns` surface would need a new external-import derivation through graph, index, and cache.

## Review

DeepWork, two rounds. The **adversarial pass refuted three claims in the first writeup**, so the harness was fixed and everything re-run rather than the prose patched. `bench/pattern_detection_results.md` ends with a six-row correction log:

1. **Wrong ground truth.** "0.00 precision on all three controls / never once found the domain" was false: `conduit.apps.core.models` was flagged and missing from my labels, and `.utils` was listed as flagged when it never was. Now 0.33 there, ground truth lives in the harness.
2. **Curation artifact.** The "4/20 corpus-C false positives" were entirely self-stack (fastapi→starlette, boto3/scrapy→botocore) plus my own `sqlite3` carve-out. `SELF_STACK` subtraction added; those four now flag zero.
3. **Overclaimed baseline.** "Contracts separate them exactly / inference loses on every axis" rested on one oracle-fed repo where `D_naming` matched its domain precision. Scoped to transitivity; fixture committed.
4. Corpus C was silently 20 of 29 (nine broken clones, disproportionately the large app-shaped ones). Repaired, now 29/29 with coverage printed.
5. `D_position_relaxed` added so the negative is not a property of one operationalization.
6. Test filter fixed; it was dropping shipped API (`fastapi.testclient`).

The verdict survived all of it. Several supporting arguments did not, and are now stated at their real strength.

Closes #288

items.title: A new opcode is cheaper than a changed one (ADR 0149)
items.body:
ADR only. **No code under `radio_server/` changed** — the host side is deliberately its own cycle. Pairs with the firmware PR: kbennett2000/uv-k1-k5v3-firmware-custom#5

## What this decides

The dock could tune the radio and could not change its demodulator. `Dock_ApplyVfo` wrote `vfo->Modulation = MODULATION_FM` on every `0x0873` (and `vfo.py:339` does the same host-side), so AM was not gated or degraded — it was **absent**.

**A new opcode `0x0877`/`0x0878`, not a 14th byte on `0x0873`.** An added field changes bytes on a frame radio-server already sends and breaks *both* directions silently: an old host's 13-byte frame is refused `ERR_SHORT` and reads as a tuning failure, and a new host's 14-byte frame decodes fine on old firmware, which then tunes on a modulation nobody set. ADR 0148 named that drift as unguarded; this declines to widen it.

## The finding that changed the opcode number

The brief specified `0x0875`. **Our own ADR 0111:52 records the classic Dock's full-control extras as *"0x0872 modulation, 0x0873/4 backlight, 0x0875/6 AM emulation"*** — so `0x0875/6` is claimed. Reading that line turned up something worse: **`0x0873/4` is on the same list**, and ADR 0140 allocated it after ruling out `0x0872` alone. That is shipped, on hardware, in 186 measured tunes, and cannot be walked back.

The census lives in three places that do not agree — `ADR 0111:52`, `ADR 0119:46`, `frames.py:113-140` — and nothing reconciles them. So `0x0877`/`0x0878`, checked against the census *before* allocating. A doc that drifts is embarrassing; a wire opcode that drifts is permanent.

## Two judgment calls beyond the brief, both confirmed before building

**The modulation is sticky and `0x0873` applies it.** Carried on **ADR 0131**, not on convenience: this link *drops frames* — the firmware is single-threaded and anything arriving while it is busy is discarded, not queued. So "tune, then set modulation" as two frames can leave the radio on the right channel in the wrong demodulator, reporting success both times. Seeded FM **from a constant, never read back off the radio** (that would be ADR 0132's fault, and would tune a repeater channel in whatever the front panel was last left on), and **a refusal never moves it**. `0x0873`'s **wire bytes are untouched** — one literal became a table lookup whose default is that literal.

**`0x0878` carries a `tx_ok` flag.** Traced rather than assumed: `GENERIC_Key_PTT` → `generic.c:192 gFlagPrepareTX` → `app.c:2612 RADIO_PrepareTX()` → `VFO_STATE_TX_DISABLE` for any non-FM modulation without `ENABLE_TX_WHEN_AM`. That is the path the **PTT pin** drives — where the `baofeng` backend keys from via the AIOC's DTR line — so **a successful set-AM stops the transmitter outright** on that station. Dock REG_30 keying bypasses it, so one firmware state means "dead transmitter" on one backend and "normal" on another, decided by a build flag a host cannot see. **`ENABLE_TX_WHEN_AM` stays off — AM is receive-only and the flag reports the condition, it does not remove it.**

## Corrections to the brief's ground truth, verified in the tree

- `RADIO_SetupAGC` takes **two** arguments (`listeningAM`, `disable`), memoises on a `static`, and returns early on a repeat.
- `0x0873`'s payload is **13** bytes (`DOCK_SET_VFO_PARAM_LEN`), not 12 — 12 is the `0x0874` reply.
- `MODULATION_UKNOWN`'s value **moves with `ENABLE_BYP_RAW_DEMODULATORS`**, which is why the wire names its own values rather than reusing the firmware enum.

Everything else in the brief verified as stated, including that the six-second TX lockout is armed at exactly four sites, none reachable from the dock dispatch.

## Verification

`uv run pytest` **1884 passed, 5 skipped** — ADR 0147's docs-contract tests accept ADR 0149 and its index row.

Firmware results are in the paired PR: fail-first **15 failures** against an always-succeeds stub and **exactly 2** against a build keeping only the `0x0873` FM hardcode, green at **98 checks / 0 failures**, FLASH **105,576 B / 118 KB (87.37%)**, +240 B.

## Not claimed

**The firmware is not flashed and no hardware result exists.** AM audio over the AIOC and the PTT refusal are new `⚠ CONFIRM AT BENCH` placeholders. Left for later cycles: the host side, the `frames.py` `SetModulation`/`0x0872` name collision, `vfo.py:339`'s own FM hardcode, and reconciling the opcode census.

items.title: feat(tools): JOO-32 - add get_station_history and get_station_baseline tools
items.body:
## Context

https://linear.app/joostkiens/issue/JOO-32/tools-get-station-history-daily-rollup-get-station-baseline

Wraps `GET /api/stations/:id/history` (daily PM2.5/weather rollup) and `GET /api/stations/:id/baseline` (365-day PM2.5 climatology), rounding out the station-scoped tool family alongside `get_station_readings`/`get_station_readings_history` (JOO-30/31).

Before writing code, I verified both routes live (read-only `curl`, station `225572`) rather than trusting the ticket/doc as-is, per CLAUDE.md's "treat `fahsai-api-reference.md` as a starting point, not ground truth." This turned up real corrections to both:

- `/history`'s response is `{ stationId, days: [...] }`, not a bare array, and the PM2.5 field is `pm25`, not `meanPm25` as both the doc and the ticket said.
- `days` caps server-side at 30 (400 above that), defaults to 7; `date` is the inclusive end-anchor, `days` counts backward from it.
- Invalid/nonexistent `station_id` doesn't 404 on either route — `/history` returns 200 with a full window of placeholder days, `/baseline` returns 200 with empty `data`/null years. Same gotcha already documented for `/station-readings/history`.
- A bug the ticket didn't mention: `pm25: 0` paired with `readingCount: 0` is the API's sentinel for "no reading ingested that day" (confirmed via a bogus `station_id` returning this pair for every day, and a real station's lapsed-feed days showing the same pair while `weather` stays non-null). Piping it straight through `classifyAqi` would misreport "Good, 0 µg/m³" for a day with no data.
- Baseline's 365-row shape (`{month, day, medianPm25, p25Pm25, p75Pm25, n}` + `minYear`/`maxYear`) matched the doc; `n` genuinely varies a lot (3–67 sampled) and the ticket's `n<30` thin-data gate is a real, common case (85/365 rows on the sampled station), not an edge case.

Also resolved with the user: the ticket's baseline default ("current-season min/median/max") needed a concrete season definition, since none existed anywhere in this codebase — the user supplied Fahsai frontend's actual `getSeason` boundaries (peak_burning Feb–Apr, early_dry Oct–Jan, monsoon May–Sep) to match rather than inventing one.

## Summary

- `src/logic/station-history.ts` + `src/tools/get-station-history.ts`: daily rollup, wind piped through `wind.ts` (never raw `windDirectionDeg`), PM2.5 through `aqi.ts`, `readingCount:0` days null out `pm25`/`aqiCategory` instead of classifying the sentinel zero, `weather`/`baseline` nulls preserved explicitly. `days` (default 7, max 30) and optional `date` enforced client-side against the live cap.
- `src/logic/station-baseline.ts` + `src/tools/get-station-baseline.ts`: default response is the current season's `{min, median, max}` of `medianPm25` plus today's specific day-of-year row; `month`+`day` (given together) return one specific day; `full: true` returns all 365 rows. Any day/aggregate built from `n < 30` samples is flagged `thin: true`. `full` wins over `month`/`day` if both given, with a note that the latter was ignored.
- Both tools require `station_id`, require it explicitly in their descriptions, and point to `get_stations` — no place/bbox input, matching `mcp-tools.md`'s checklist for station-scoped tools.
- Wired into `src/index.ts`.
- `docs/claude/fahsai-api-reference.md` corrected in place with all the live findings above, dated to this session.
- `docs/claude/conventions.md`: documented this repo's actual branch-naming template (`<type>(<scope>)/<linear-branch-slug>`, e.g. `feat(tools)/joo-32-...`) — it wasn't written down anywhere, and I'd initially miscopied a `worktree-` prefix from recent branches that turned out to be a tooling artifact, not the convention.

**Addressed in a follow-up commit after `/code-review`:**

- `get_station_baseline` was returning `medianPm25`/`p25Pm25`/`p75Pm25` (and the season `min`/`median`/`max` aggregates) as bare numbers with no `aqiCategory` — a violation of CLAUDE.md's non-negotiable "every PM2.5 value carries an AQI category" rule. `get_station_history`'s passthrough of the per-day `baseline` stat had the same gap. Both now classify every PM2.5 value (median, p25, p75, and each season aggregate) individually.
- `toStationHistoryDay` only guarded `weather`/`baseline` against `null`, not `undefined` — since `fahsai-client` casts parsed JSON straight through with no runtime check, a response that omits either key entirely (rather than sending explicit `null`) would have thrown inside `.map()` and aborted the whole call. Fixed to treat missing and explicit-null the same.
- `parseWindDir` was called directly on `windDirectionDeg`, which throws `RangeError` for any non-finite value — the same unvalidated-JSON risk, with no defensive handling. Added `parseWindDirOrNull` to `wind.ts` (mirroring `aqi.ts`'s existing `classifyAqiOrNull`) and used it here.
- `get_station_history`'s empty-`days` branch returned no explanatory note, unlike the sibling `get_station_readings_history` tool's established convention for the same zero-results case. Added one.
- Refactored `station-baseline.ts`'s three near-identical `data.length === 0` no-data guards (in `summarizeStationBaselineDefault`/`Day`/`Full`) into one shared `emptyBaselineSummary` helper.
- Added test coverage for all of the above (malformed/missing weather-baseline keys, non-finite wind direction, the new empty-days note, and "never a bare PM2.5 number without a category" checks in both logic modules).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` / `npm run build` clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 180 tests pass (174 + 6 new from the code-review fixes), no network involved
- [x] Manual smoke test of the built handlers against the live API, re-run after the fixes: `get_station_history` (good station `225572` defaults, a past-date window, and a bogus station_id) and `get_station_baseline` (default season+today, a specific day, `full: true`, and a bogus station_id) all match the verified findings above, now with an `aqiCategory` on every PM2.5 value

items.title: Audit CLAUDE.md: correct six false claims, cut historical narrative
items.body:
**TL;DR** Line-by-line audit of `CLAUDE.md` against the code. **Six claims were false**, including one whole section describing a checkout that does not exist and one that overstates what `methods/` contains by five baselines. Also cut five passages of historical narrative that justified decisions already made. **No new guidance added.** +75/−89, net −14 lines. Stacked on #86.

## Question / goal

Make every claim in `CLAUDE.md` true, and remove what no longer earns its space.

## Background

`CLAUDE.md` is loaded into context every session and is the single highest-leverage document in the repo — a false claim in it propagates into every subagent brief. It had grown to 542 lines across many sessions, and parts of it were written against a codebase state that has since moved. Two recent incidents came from exactly this: a brief told four agents the upstream pylint plugin bans `np.random` (it does not), and this file still instructed everyone to pin `reference/kinder-baselines` to a branch that had been merged away.

## Hypothesis

None — documentation audit, not an experiment.

## Guidance given

Go through it line by line; correct anything fake; remove anything extra or obsolete; **do not add new things**.

## Methods

Read the file end to end, then checked every falsifiable claim against the tree: directory and file existence, CI job structure in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, exported names in the `types.py` files it enumerates, the `run_task_episode` signature, registered `--env`/`--method` names in `cli.py`, the Tossing Room test composition, `du` on `reference/`, and the `kinder/__init__.py` line reference.

## Results

**Six false claims, all corrected:**

| Claim | Reality |
|---|---|
| `reference/` is ~1.9 GB | **4.4 GB** |
| "All four of lint/typecheck/import-direction/test run in CI… the same four commands" | **Three jobs** running **five** commands — `lint` bundles `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `lint-imports` |
| `methods/practice_makes_perfect/` "reproduces the paper's method + every baseline it compares against (Fail Focus, Competence Gradient, Skill Diversity, Task-Relevant, Task Repeat, Random Skills, MAPLE-Q)" | Contains **`ees_method.py` and `random_skills_method.py` only**. The other five are not implemented |
| `humans/` "— concrete `HumanOracle` implementations" | **Empty** — a README and an `__init__.py`. This is *why* `Metrics.num_human_interventions()` reports nothing |
| `core/method/types.py` exports 8 named types | Also exports **`SetupCommandTarget`** |
| A whole section on `../hitl-practice`, "one directory up" | **Not present on this machine**, anywhere under `~/Documents/repos`. The section now points at `reference/predicators`, which does have `envs/grid_row.py`, `ground_truth_models/grid_row/` and `settings.py` |

The `hitl-practice` correction is the one worth a second look: the guidance itself is good and the files it names are all reachable at `reference/predicators`, so I repointed rather than deleted, and left a line saying where the pointer used to go in case that fork exists somewhere.

**Five passages removed**, all of them justification for decisions long since made rather than instruction: the static-method-container history in the `core/` section, the `Metrics` shared-`ClassVar`-plus-`reset()` history, the IKFast wheel-library retraction anecdote, the macOS `gtimeout` aside on a Linux-only project, and the nest-under-`problem/` rationale that restated what it then points at `core/README.md` for.

**Claims checked and confirmed true**, so left alone: the Tossing Room 14/14/2 test composition, `run_task_episode`'s `(succeeded, frames)` return, `core/problem/human/types.py`'s three exports, `kinder/__init__.py:67-74`'s `osmesa` forcing, the named single-test example, `recording/README.md`'s four reset kinds, and every file path in the Architecture section other than the ones above.

**Net −14 lines**, which is less shrinkage than the removals alone would give: the corrections to `humans/` and `methods/` needed *more* words than the false versions, because stating what is absent takes longer than implying it is present. I erred toward keeping operational detail — the traps and gate instructions were all earned the hard way.

Gate: docs-only, no code in the diff, so the code gate is not informative here and was not run.

## Recommendation

Merge after #84 and #86.

One judgement call to check: I treated the `core/` and `Metrics` design *history* as extra, on the grounds that the rule it justifies is stated right next to it. If you want that rationale preserved somewhere rather than dropped, `core/README.md` is the natural home and I can move it there instead.

items.title: Add stem quality probe for separator feasibility testing
items.body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a new feasibility probe (`stem_quality_probe.py`) and accompanying GitHub Actions workflow to evaluate whether lower-quality vocal separators (suitable for real-time/browser-grade use) can still produce stems clean enough for the energy-onset detector to reliably find verse markers. The probe runs the same detection pipeline on stems from two separators (Demucs as reference, Open-Unmix as proxy) and compares results head-to-head.

## Key Changes

- **New module: `tooling/stem_quality_probe.py`**
  - Standalone feasibility experiment comparing Demucs (high-quality, offline-only reference) vs Open-Unmix umxhq (lighter, lower-quality proxy for real-time/browser separation)
  - Reuses existing detection pipeline from `detect_first_verse` and `raw_onset_probe` to ensure identical signal processing on both stems
  - Implements Open-Unmix separation via soundfile/torch (avoiding torchaudio CLI quirks)
  - Computes vocal-vs-jam energy contrast as a measure of stem quality and detector headroom
  - Generates both Markdown and JSON reports with detailed comparison metrics
  - CLI interface for flexible testing with custom audio, ground-truth files, and parameters

- **New GitHub Actions workflow: `.github/workflows/stem-quality-probe.yml`**
  - Manual trigger workflow for running the probe on arbitrary audio files
  - Accepts inputs: audio URL (with Dropbox auto-correction), song ID, ground-truth path, and song offset
  - Installs CPU-only PyTorch and required dependencies (demucs, openunmix, librosa, scipy, soundfile)
  - Caches torch hub models for faster repeated runs
  - Uploads probe reports (Markdown, JSON, stdout) as artifacts
  - Appends Markdown report to GitHub job summary for easy visibility

## Implementation Details

- **Separation pipeline**: Both separators receive identical 44.1 kHz stereo WAV input via ffmpeg normalization
- **Detection reuse**: Imports and reuses `_separate_vocals`, `_smoothed_envelope`, `_vocal_stem_rms_db` from `detect_first_verse` and detection/scoring functions from `raw_onset_probe` to ensure consistency
- **Contrast metric**: Computes mean stem energy over verse sections minus mean over jam sections—a direct measure of how much headroom the detector has
- **Verdict criteria**: Checks if Open-Unmix detects verse_5 within ±5s tolerance and reports contrast loss vs Demucs reference
- **Reporting**: Generates comparison tables, detailed verdicts, and per-separator envelope/detection data in both human-readable and machine-parseable formats

items.title: Geo filters: implement for VectorSets, Milvus and MongoDB; pin Chroma/Turbopuffer as real gaps (#223)
items.body:
Two shipped datasets — `random-geo-radius-100-angular-filters` and
`random-geo-radius-2048-angular-filters` — carry
`{"<field>": {"geo": {"lon", "lat", "radius"}}}` conditions with geo-filtered ground
truth. Five engines dropped that leaf: before #251 they searched **unfiltered** and
published the result as filtered recall; since #251 they **abort**, so the two
datasets are unrunnable on them. (Four datasets are geo-*named*; the two
`-no-filters` twins are `"conditions": null` throughout and were never affected.)

This restores three of the five using each engine's own capability, and pins the
other two as permanent, evidenced gaps rather than to-dos.

## Per-engine disposition

| engine | disposition | mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **vectorsets** | implemented | the point is stored as its **unit vector on the sphere** in three top-level attributes; `FILTER` evaluates `(.f__geo_x*qx + .f__geo_y*qy + .f__geo_z*qz) >= cos(r/R)` |
| **milvus** | implemented | native **`Geometry`** column (WKT `POINT(lon lat)`) + `RTREE` index, filtered with **`ST_DWITHIN(field, 'POINT(lon lat)', metres)`** |
| **mongodb** | implemented | **`$search` + the `vectorSearch` operator** with a `geoWithin`/`circle` **pre-filter** over a `search`-type index — used *only* for geo-carrying datasets |
| **chroma** | genuinely impossible | see below |
| **turbopuffer** | genuinely impossible | see below |
| **dragonfly** | *newly* refused | shared-builder gap: Dragonfly Search **does** do geo, but rejects this repo's `$param` placeholders and integer literals, so no GEO field is declared |
| **valkey** | *newly* refused | engine gap: Valkey Search has no GEO field type; the emitted clause was rejected at query time |

### VectorSets — exact, without a geo type

`VSIM … FILTER` has no geo type and **no function calls at all** (no `sqrt`, no
trigonometry), so haversine is not writable. It does have `*`, `+` and `>=` over
several top-level attributes at once, and that is all an *exact* great-circle test
needs. For unit vectors `u`, `q` on the sphere, `u·q` **is** the cosine of the central
angle, so

```
great-circle distance(u, q) <= r   ⟺   u·q >= cos(r / R)
```

The right-hand side is a per-query constant; the left is a linear form over three
stored scalars. `engine/geo.rs` holds the maths, with a test that compares the
predicate against haversine metres over a grid of point pairs × radii (poles and
antimeridian included) and a test that a bounding-box corner is rejected.

This is **not** a bounding box and not an equirectangular approximation. The point
used to be stored as the nested object `{"lon":…,"lat":…}`, which `FILTER` cannot read
at all — selectors reach only top-level keys and a non-scalar makes the whole
expression false — so the data was on the server and unusable.

### Milvus — native, and it was never merely "unfiltered"

`geo` now maps to a `Geometry` column (Milvus ≥ 2.6.4; the pinned test image is
v2.6.19) with the only index type it offers, `RTREE`, and the filter is
`ST_DWITHIN`. For a POINT column against a POINT query the server computes a
**haversine great-circle distance on R = 6 371 000 m** and compares `<= radius`
(`internal/core/src/common/Geometry.h::dwithin`) — the same earth radius
`geo::EARTH_RADIUS_M` and the fixtures' ground truth use.

**Correction to the issue.** #223 lists Milvus as "runs unfiltered". Measured on
master it does not get that far: `geo` materialised **no column**, upload still
emitted the key, and with `enableDynamicField: false` the insert is rejected —
`Insert failed: fail to deal the insert data, error: has pass more field without
dynamic schema`. So the Milvus RED is an upload failure, not a silent recall. The
stored value was also wrong twice over: `"{lat},{lon}"`, where WKT wants
`POINT(lon lat)`.

### MongoDB — a different stage, not a different operator

`$vectorSearch`'s `filter` is MQL restricted to ten comparison operators and rejects
geo outright. Verified live against `mongodb/mongodb-atlas-local:8.0.17`:

```
$vectorSearch + {loc: {$geoWithin: {$centerSphere: [[-74,40], r/R]}}}
  → PlanExecutor error … "filter.loc" at least one of
    [$gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $eq, $ne, $in, $nin, $exists, $not] must be present
```

and a `vectorSearch`-type index has no geo field type. MongoDB's geo-capable vector
**pre-filter** is the `vectorSearch` *operator* inside a `$search` stage over a
`search`-type index, whose `filter` takes a MongoDB Search operator tree and therefore
`geoWithin` with a `circle`. That path returns exactly the in-radius documents on the
same image.

So the engine now picks its stage from the dataset schema (`schema_declares_geo`):
geo-carrying datasets get the `$search` path and a `search`-type index; **everything
else is byte-identical to before**, so no existing MongoDB number moves. The HNSW
build knobs carry over unchanged — `hnswOptions.{maxEdges,numEdgeCandidates}` are
honoured by the `search`-type index too (checked by reading `latestDefinition` back).

Deliberately **not** used: a `$match` after `$vectorSearch`. That is a post-filter —
it shrinks the k results the stage already returned — so it would depress recall in a
way that is not comparable with the pre-filtering engines. The `filter-only`
(`find()`) path keeps MQL and gains a real `$geoWithin`/`$centerSphere` arm, which
works there with no `2dsphere` index (verified live).

### Chroma and Turbopuffer — refused, permanently

Both filter DSLs are a **closed enum of `field OP literal` comparisons**:

* Chroma `where`: `$eq $ne $gt $gte $lt $lte $in $nin $and $or`, over scalar metadata
  only. ([docs](https://docs.trychroma.com/docs/querying-collections/metadata-filtering))
* Turbopuffer: `Eq NotEq In NotIn Lt Lte Gt Gte Any* Contains* Glob* Regex
  ContainsAllTokens ContainsAnyToken ContainsTokenSequence Fuzzy And Or Not`, and its
  attribute types are `string/int/uint/float/uuid/datetime/bool` (+ arrays) — no geo
  and no struct type. ([query](https://turbopuffer.com/docs/query),
  [schema](https://turbopuffer.com/docs/schema))

Neither has a geo primitive, an attribute-on-the-right-hand-side, or arithmetic
anywhere in the filter grammar. (Turbopuffer *does* have arithmetic — in `rank_by`,
which its docs state never affects matching, so it cannot exclude a document.) That
rules out every exact encoding: a spherical cap is not an axis-aligned box in any
*query-independent* coordinate system, so no conjunction of ranges carves it out, and
the linear dot-product form VectorSets uses needs cross-field arithmetic neither has.
A bounding box would admit points up to √2·r away — a filter that looks applied and
under-constrains, which is exactly what #219 exists to stop.

Their `KNOWN_GAPS` entries stay, with that reasoning attached. One real fix went in
alongside: **a condition tree containing a geo leaf is now refused *whole***. Both
builders keep the leaves they understand, so `and(geo, keyword)` previously emitted
just the keyword clause — a real-looking filter that constrains less than the ground
truth does, and one that passes the #219 guard. (Not reachable on shipped data, which
is geo-only, but it is the partial-drop escape `query_filter.rs` documents.)

## Dragonfly and Valkey — holes this PR would otherwise have made worse

`dragonfly::configure()` deliberately never declares a GEO field (Dragonfly Search's
geo-query parser rejects the `$param` placeholders the shared RediSearch builder
emits), but `search()` called `redis::parse_conditions` **directly**, so it happily
emitted `@f:[$lon $lat $r m]` against a field that does not exist. Pre-existing and
silent — and this PR's `filter_guard` turned it into three **asserted-green** cells, in
the one file whose job is catching exactly this. `dragonfly::parse_conditions` now
refuses any tree mentioning geo, the matrix column calls it, and the cells are tracked
gaps. Also corrected in the README and the `filter_guard` header, both of which this PR
had wrongly listed Dragonfly among the geo-expressing engines.

**Valkey is the same shape, one column over**, found by a sibling sweep rather than by
me. Valkey Search has no GEO field type, so `configure()` adds none — but `build_leaf`'s
`"geo"` arm still emitted `@f:[$lon $lat $r m]`, the matrix scored all three geo shapes
FILTERED with no tracked gap, and this PR's own new `KNOWN_GAPS` prose and README
paragraph both named Valkey as geo-capable. Live, it hard-errors at query time
(`'location' is not indexed as a numeric field`), so it was a mid-run failure after a
full ingest rather than silent wrong recall — now refused up front.

The two gaps are **not the same kind**, and the `KNOWN_GAPS` reasons now say so:
Dragonfly Search genuinely supports geo (`@loc:[20.0 10.0 500000.0 m]` returns results
on a real GEO attribute); what it rejects is this repo's `$param` placeholders and
integer literals, so teaching the shared builder to inline float literals would close
it. Valkey's is a real engine gap.

Split is now **(232, 23)**, `KNOWN_GAPS` 23.

## Undisclosed fixture blind spots, now closed

* **A lat/lon swap applied to both sides is invisible.** Self-consistent, so it selects
  the identical documents — the single most likely geo bug class (WKT `POINT(x y)` vs
  GeoJSON `[lon,lat]`). The query side was pinned; Milvus' *insert* side was not.
  Extracted `geo_wkt_point` and pinned it, plus that storage and query agree.
* **The in-circle set was exactly one upload batch.** In-circle was ids 0..99 and
  `batch_size` is 100 in the Milvus and MongoDB geo configs, so any failure leaving only
  the first batch resident would score 1.000 with **no geo filter at all**. In-circle is
  now `id.is_multiple_of(4)`, interleaved — landed in `df790b1` after `dba6f23` claimed
  it without it being in the tree (see that commit's message).
* All 10 corner queries share one centre and one radius, so a hard-coded centre passes
  there; `write_geo_edge_project` is the fixture that varies the centre.

## RED → GREEN, on live servers

All runs on containers started for this branch (redis `7399`, milvus `19541`, mongodb
`27028`, chroma `8013`) with a private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. RED = `src/` reverted to
master `01145d4` with the new fixtures in place.

| test | RED (master `01145d4`) | GREEN (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| `test_binary_vectorsets_geo` | FAILED — `VectorSets cannot express the filter on query 0 … would search UNFILTERED … (issue #219)` | **recall = 1.000** |
| `test_binary_milvus_geo` | FAILED — `Insert failed: … has pass more field without dynamic schema` | **recall = 1.000**, and the read-back shows the `Geometry` column present with **no scalar index** (only `vector: HNSW, 400/400`) |
| `test_binary_mongodb_geo` | FAILED — `MongoDB cannot express the filter on query 0 … would search UNFILTERED … (issue #219)` | **recall = 1.000**, and `$listSearchIndexes` reports `type: "search"` |
| `test_binary_chroma_geo_is_refused_loudly` | passes (chroma refuses on master too) | passes — still a nonzero exit carrying `UNFILTERED` / `#219` / `Chroma cannot express the filter` |
| `test_binary_redis_geo_corner` (**control**) | **recall = 1.000** | **recall = 1.000** |

## Review round 2 — two blockers fixed

**VectorSets hard-errored on 25 of the 10 000 shipped queries.** `{:?}` switches to
exponent form below `1e-4` and VectorSets' `exprParseNumber` accepts a *leading* `-`
but not the one after `e`, so a centre within ~0.006° of the equator or a meridian
failed the whole query (`ERR syntax error … near: -5 + …`). New `geo::plain_decimal`
emits the shortest fixed-point form that round-trips, never exponent form; Milvus'
WKT literals go through it too. Tested against both real shipped centres and a sweep
to the smallest subnormal.

**Milvus' `RTREE` on a `Geometry` column prunes with a box SMALLER than the cap.**
`create_bounding_box_for_dwithin` divides by `111320.0` m/deg where the truth is
111 194.93, so the box is ~0.11 % short in every direction, and it never wraps the
antimeridian — true hits are discarded before the exact refine runs. Reproduced
first-hand on v2.6.19, identical rows in two collections differing only by the index:

| case | truth | with RTREE | no index |
|---|---|---|---|
| centre (81, 10), r = 200 km | 20 docs | **14** (the six at 0.9990–0.9995·r due N/S) | 20 |
| centre (0, 179.9), r = 200 km | 8 docs | **4** (every doc across +180) | 8 |

On the edge fixture's own 400 rows the prune removes **74 of 150** in-cap documents on
q0 and **38 of 150** on q1. The column is now materialised but **deliberately
unindexed** — the one exception to the #218 column-implies-index rule, with
`MilvusFieldKind::index_type` an `Option` and the exception set pinned to exactly
`{geo}` by `only_geo_is_a_deliberately_unindexed_column`. `ST_DWITHIN` alone is exact.

**Why the harness still scores 1.000 with the index — the real reason, after two wrong
ones.** I first wrote "the ~6 pruned documents rarely reach the top-10" (the pruned set
is 74 and 38 documents, not ~6) and a reviewer proposed "the vector-search path ignores
the prune" (it does not). Isolating the variable:

| index created | `entities/query` | `entities/search` |
|---|---|---|
| in `collections/create`'s `indexParams`, **before** insert | 76 / 150 | 76 / 150 |
| via `indexes/create`, **after** insert + flush (this engine's order) | 150 / 150 | 150 / 150 |

So the prune is honoured on both paths, and what decides it is **index creation
order**. This engine indexes after insert, which is why the RTREE was invisible at 400
rows. That is an artifact of ordering at this size, not a guarantee — which is exactly
why the column is left unindexed rather than relying on it.

The `806/12 500` (6.4 %) and `~0.935 ceiling` figures are a **model of the box formula
/ a `query`-path result**, not a measured search recall; labelled as such.

`assert_geo_column_present_and_unindexed` is the assertion that fires (verified by
re-adding the index: `'location' must stay UNINDEXED`). Its "column exists" branch is
defence-in-depth, not the live guard for master's regression — that one dies at INSERT
and never reaches the function.

## Two claims that had nothing checking them

* **Chroma's whole-tree geo refusal** could be deleted with all tests green, because
  the integration fixture is geo-only so the leaf builder refuses anyway. Now pinned:
  `and(geo, keyword)` → `None` for *both* builders (plus the full-text sibling and the
  nested case), and the test first shows the sibling alone renders, so `None` is the
  guard and not an inability.
* **`filter_guard`'s MongoDB dialect routing** could be forced to MQL with the matrix
  unchanged. Now pinned: the two grammars are shown to differ, and a geo schema must
  select `$search`.

## The fixture, and why it is not a bounding-box pass

The existing `write_geo_project` puts all 400 documents on **one meridian**, where a
lat/lon box and a great-circle circle select the identical set. It proves a geo filter
was applied; it cannot tell a correct radius from a box.

`write_geo_corner_project` (new, L2 + cosine variants) is built to fail a box. All 400
documents sit inside the query's bounding box, but:

* **100** are within 0.71·radius of the centre — inside the circle;
* **300** sit in the four corner regions, each ≥ 1.10·radius away — outside it.

Ground truth is the top-10 over the 100 in-circle documents (**selectivity 25 %**,
ground-truth width 10, `matching_docs = 100 ≫ top = 10`). A correct radius scores
~1.0; a bounding box, or no filter at all, searches all 400 and keeps roughly a
quarter of the correct neighbours — **≈ 0.25 by construction**, far under the 0.9 floor
these tests assert. No document is within 5 % of the boundary, so no engine's earth
model can move one across it; the builder asserts the box-containment, the margin and
both counts rather than trusting the layout arithmetic.

The **Redis control** (`test_binary_redis_geo_corner`) runs the same fixture against
RediSearch's already-correct native `@f:[lon lat r m]` and scores 1.000 — so a failure
on the three fixed engines is the engine, not the fixture.

**What the corner fixture is blind to**, stated so nobody over-reads it. Its guard band
is `[0.7065, 1.1013]·r`, so any radius within `[−29.4 %, +10.1 %]` selects the identical
100 documents — a wrong radius is a provably equivalent mutant here (×1.101 → 100 docs,
×1.11 → 104, ×1.15 → 128, ×1.40 → 400). So is `>` vs `>=`, and so is an equirectangular
approximation (~1e-5 relative error at 20 km). Those are caught by the exact-string unit
pins and by `geo.rs`'s poles-and-antimeridian haversine grid — **the "not an
equirectangular approximation" claim is earned by that grid, not by the fixture.** Being
blind in both directions is also why it cannot see a prune box *smaller* than the cap,
which is what `write_geo_edge_project` (81 N near-boundary + antimeridian) exists for.

**This retroactively weakens every prior geo assertion in this repo.** Repointing a geo
test at the old `write_geo_project` and swapping the engine's predicate for a real
lat/lon polygon still scores **1.000**; the same mutant scores **0.240** on the corner
fixture. So `test_binary_redis_geo` and its siblings prove "a geo-ish filter was
applied", never "the shape is a circle". That is an argument for this change, not
against it. (Its comment also claimed a "~55 m" margin; the true tightest is 16.6 m —
corrected.)

## Verifying the query on the wire, not just the recall

* **Milvus** — the unit test pins the exact emitted string
  (`ST_DWITHIN(loc, 'POINT(10.0 20.0)', 500.0)`, longitude first), and the integration
  test reads the server's own index catalogue back (`RTREE`, 400/400 rows).
* **MongoDB** — unit tests pin the emitted `geoWithin.circle` document (centre
  `[lon, lat]`, radius in metres) and the `$search`/`searchScore` pipeline shape; the
  integration test asserts the index MongoDB actually built is `type: "search"`.
* **VectorSets** — a unit test parses the coefficients and threshold **back out of the
  rendered expression** (what the server would read) and checks the predicate against
  haversine metres over a grid, including a bounding-box corner that must be rejected.
* `filter_guard`'s matrix prints the rendered filter per engine per shipped shape, and
  `no_shipped_multi_leaf_filter_loses_a_leaf` confirms both leaves of `and_geo_x2` /
  `or_geo_x2` survive.

## Doc corrections from review

* The shipped ground truth uses **R = 6 371 008.8** (qdrant's
  `ann-filtering-benchmark-datasets`, `_AVG_EARTH_RADIUS_KM = 6371.0088`, strict `<`),
  not our 6 371 000. Kept at 6 371 000 for consistency with the repo fixtures and with
  Milvus' own refine step, because a *smaller* R makes our cap a strict **superset** —
  no ground-truth neighbour can ever be excluded, and the cost is 24 extra admitted
  documents across 500 queries (0.048/query against ~13 810 matching docs/query).
* Shipped radii are **1 193 – 1 991 786 m** (mean 990 613), not "~3·10⁵".
* Precision figures replaced with measured crossover values: **7 µm** worst case at the
  1 193 m end, ~1e-8 m at the mean, 4.2 mm at a hand-written r = 1 m. Server-side
  arithmetic confirmed `double`, not f32 (which would have been worth ±2.4 km at
  r = 1 000 m).
* Noted the one place the encoding is not literally exact: at r = 0 a document exactly
  at the centre gives `dot(u,u) = 0.999999999999999 9` and is excluded. Unreachable on
  shipped data (min radius 1 193 m).
* README's "moving the check earlier for the other five" is now two engines.

## `filter_guard` bookkeeping

`KNOWN_GAPS` shrinks 26 → 17 (nine geo entries removed: vectorsets/milvus/mongodb ×
`and_geo`, `and_geo_x2`, `or_geo_x2`), and the expressible/refused split moves
**(229, 26) → (238, 17)**. The guard asserts in both directions, so those nine could
not have been removed without the builders actually resolving. MongoDB's column in the
matrix now routes by schema exactly as production does, so the geo shapes are tested
through the dialect that would really be sent.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo test --lib --bins` and `cargo test --test overhead_invariants` are all clean on
the merge commit. Totals are in the comments below.

`engine/geo.rs` is also added to INV-4b's `EXCUSED` list: it is a 359-line pure helper
with no `impl Engine for`, so it has no timed search to gate. The guard's message
("the synchronized start is gone") reads as a regression for a file that never had a
gate, and its `EXCUSED` list has to be hand-fed for every future non-engine module —
both filed as #287 against #263's guard rather than patched here.

## Deliberately left out

* **No bounding-box fallback anywhere.** A widened filter is worse than a refusal.
* **`datetime` in MongoDB's `search`-index mapping is an `Err`, not a guess.**
  `metadata_value_to_bson` stores datetimes as the raw ISO *string*, so neither
  `number` nor `date` would match, and a lexicographic `token` range was not verified
  live. No shipped dataset carries geo and datetime together, so the arm is
  unreachable today.
* **Turbopuffer has no live run** — it is cloud-only with no emulator or self-hosted
  build, so its evidence is documentation plus unit tests. MongoDB's MQL
  `$centerSphere` arm (the `find()`/filter-only path) likewise has only a unit
  string pin, though the operator itself was verified live in `mongosh`.
* **Not re-tuning the corner fixture to catch radius error.** It would need a document
  band tighter than the cross-engine earth-radius spread, which would make it
  engine-specific; the exact-string pins cover it instead.
* **The refusal still happens in `search()`**, after `configure()` and `upload()`, for
  chroma/turbopuffer. Moving it earlier is the pre-existing follow-up noted in the
  README.
* Untouched by design: `experiment.rs` / `effective_config.rs` (#264) and the
  skip-flag / `corpus_row_count` paths (#271).

Closes #223

items.title: release: v2026.5.8 — pairing access modes, PWA, mobile consolidation, HUP fixes
items.body:
## Summary

Closes the 21 issues catalogued in `.internal/audit-v2026.5.5/A4-map.md` §4 (8 critical, 11 major, 2 minor) by separating the four concerns that the previous code conflated under "pairing":

1. **Brain reachability** — picks one of three modes (`local` / `localhost` / `remote`) and emits a Mode-aware pair URL. The `_pair_payload` rewrite consults `runtime.brain_public_base_url()` and the new `access.pairing_mode` setting. The hardcoded `port = 9090` literal is gone.
2. **Device pairing identity** — Argon2id + SHA-256 + 24h sliding-TTL token lifecycle preserved verbatim; the new code-pair flow (8-char base32 codes, 5-attempts/15min/IP rate limit) is layered on top.
3. **Owner/account identity** — design-only this PR (see `SECURITY.md`). No `owner.*` settings keys touched.
4. **Bridge topology** — phone bridges glasses/wristband; brain bridges appliances via skills. One paragraph in the design doc; no code change.

Plus:
- The `/setup` wizard gained a **Pair your phone** step (with a `Skip for now` exit) and now correctly POSTs `/api/setup/complete`.
- PWA scaffolding (manifest, icons, service worker with auth-sensitive bypass).
- HUP protocol bumped to v1.2.0: `node_heartbeat`, `node_ack`, `hup_action_request`, `hup_action_response`, `node_bye`, `error` are canonical; `command`/`execute`/`hup_execute` are deprecated aliases until 2026.7.0.
- Mobile consolidation: deleted `apps/{ios,android}` and `feral-nodes/android-app/` (all unpublished); promoted `feral-nodes/android-bridge/sample/` to `ai.feral.app`; `feral-nodes/ios-app/` is the iOS app of record. Both got `feral://` deep-link registration and a unified QR v1 decoder with backward-compat for legacy shapes.
- Phone-bridge migrated to `Authorization: Bearer` with a graceful fallback to `?api_key=` during the deprecation window.
- `/api/...` honest 404s — the SPA catch-all no longer masks unknown API routes with HTML.
- New CLI / endpoint / settings: `access.pairing_mode`, `access.tailscale.tailnet_url`, `access.remote_provider`, `meta.brain_id`, `POST /api/devices/pair/{announce,code/claim}`, `GET /api/devices/pair/status`, plus a new in-process rate limiter at `feral-core/api/middleware/rate_limit.py`.

Audit artifacts — `A4-repro.md` (Phase 0 evidence), `A4-map.md` (Phase 1 single-source-of-truth), `A4-pairing-redesign.md` (Phase 2 design with the BLOCKER + 4 MAJORs from inline self-review applied) — live under `.internal/audit-v2026.5.5/` and are intentionally NOT in this diff (internal scratch dir).

## Out of scope (deliberately deferred)

- Tailscale CLI integration (`feral access remote-up`, `feral pair-mode`) — designed in `A4-pairing-redesign.md` §2 but not implemented here. The `access.pairing_mode = "remote"` resolver IS plumbed; switching from `localhost` → `remote` requires a manual `FERAL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` until the CLI lands. Tracked as a follow-up. Mode A and Mode B are end-to-end functional today.
- `feral-client/` v1 tree — kept untouched. The `/setup/legacy` route INSIDE v2 is removed (legacy `SetupWizard.jsx`); the v1 codebase under `feral-client/` is a separate concern (referenced as a CHANGELOG follow-up).

items.title: Alpha + skill-improvement guides: worktree setup, viewer, Windows parity
items.body:
Three walkthrough docs had drifted from how the loop is actually run. From a read-through with Dallan.

## What changed

**Worktree and working directory.** Neither example said where to stand. Both now open with `make install-hooks` + `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch>`, and state which directory each surface opens in.

This matters most in the feedback loop, where two directories are live at once: terminals and the skill-improver run in the **worktree**, but Claude Code for steps 3–5 runs in the **unpacked case folder**. `setup-feedback-case.sh` stamps `.feedback-repo-root` from wherever it's invoked, and that marker decides where the mined test lands — so the branch has to exist *before* the case is unpacked. Ordered accordingly as a new Step 0.

**Research Viewer.** Both docs described noticing and confirming a defect from the chat transcript alone. The "notice" and "confirm" steps now launch the viewer (`make electron`) on the same project folder, with the reason it matters in each case: the citation defect *is* a string in the research log; the unproven-parent defect *is* an assertion in the tree.

**Windows parity.** The genealogists on the team run the `.bat` files, not `make`. Every make command in both docs now carries its batch equivalent. Two gaps filled:
- `make feedback-case` — a target over the existing `scripts/setup-feedback-case.sh`, which had none
- `eval/GateSkill.bat` — did not exist; added and listed in `eval/README.md` + `eval/CLAUDE.md`

**Why `gate-skill` exists.** The question was whether we could delete it and just re-run `eval-skill` and compare. No — and both docs now say why:
- it runs **one side**, reading the "before" scores from the step-4 run log with human `.ann` corrections overlaid, so the baseline is ground truth rather than a second n=1 judge draw
- it covers the mined test + holdouts, so it's seconds and you can iterate on the edit
- it distinguishes **INCONCLUSIVE** (the bug never reproduced on the un-edited skill, so nothing was proven) from a fix that didn't land. A score diff shows two passing runs and lets you conclude, wrongly, that you're done.

**One skill per PR, softened.** Some fixes genuinely span skills — a doctrine change about evidence classification has to land in `person-evidence`, `conflict-resolution` and `proof-conclusion` together or they contradict each other mid-research. Both docs now say one *problem* per PR, and note the runlog gate checks every skill a PR touches.

**`alpha-user-guide`: "pick a real brick wall" replaced.** Alpha testers are professional genealogists whose actual brick walls are far beyond the agent, and failing one teaches us nothing. Replaced with two explicit paths for choosing a research objective — (A) own research not on FamilySearch, supplying starting point + objective; (B) a FamilySearch PID with something specified to forget. The old "practising on a solved question" section was path B described in passing, so it's folded in rather than left duplicated.

Also drops two stale lines: the model-picker note and the "a wiki page lookup fails" troubleshooting row.

## Verification

Wiki tools smoke-tested live against the hosted `wiki-query-api`, which is what justified dropping that troubleshooting row:

| Tool | Result |
|---|---|
| `wiki_search` | 1,240,565 chunks searched, ranked results at 0.78–0.84 relevance |
| `wiki_read` | `Italy_Civil_Registration`, 59,414 chars |
| `wiki_place_page` | "Italy" + `online_records` resolved to the right page, 12,537 chars |

`make feedback-case` checked both ways (missing-`ZIP` error path and `make -n` expansion). Docs-only otherwise — no code paths touched, and none of the changed `eval/` files are on a `check-runlogs.yml` trigger path.

## Not in this PR

A Sonnet 5 upgrade was drafted and reverted — we want a proper comparison first, particularly because the parent orchestrator has never run on Sonnet 5 in this app and the runaway-thinking failure that got `record-extractor` pinned back to 4.6 was Sonnet-5-specific. Default stays `claude-sonnet-4-6`.

Open question left in the docs: the "Only one model" line is now gone from the alpha guide, but testers still see a single-entry model dropdown. Happy to put a corrected version back if you'd rather name it.
