items.title: feat(mt#3547): Give the reviewer permission to stop: per-round tool-budget counter

labels.name: authorship/co-authored
labels.description: Co-authored by human and AI agent

items.body:
# Summary

The reviewer burns its whole tool-loop budget and then has to be told to stop. Across the 8 days
ending 2026-08-01, **730 of 871 reviews (84%) ran to exactly the 10-round cap**, costing $201.84 —
70% of the $289.35 total. The model does not emit `conclude_review` in-loop; a forced 11th call
extracts the verdict, and two reviews sampled live during planning both logged `fired_at_turn=10`.

The cause is structural, not a tuning problem. The prompt pairs an unbounded coverage mandate
(Principle 11: *"You must review 100% of the diff before concluding"*) with a stop signal whose
satisfaction is conditional on it (*"your FINAL tool call MUST be `conclude_review`"*, after
emitting everything else). That is OpenAI's documented **persistence pattern** — the recipe for
*increasing* exhaustive tool use — and it reads as "not yet, forever."

This PR ships the mechanism and the harness to validate it. **The A/B ran, the hypothesis failed
on its stated criterion (round count did not move), and two other effects appeared — one large.**
A second measurement round (finding-level diff, conclude-round instrumentation, cap=6 experiment,
cost conversion) firmed the picture; the principal decided **ship and watch production**
(ask#6768, answered 2026-08-03). See Live verification.

# What changed

**`prompt.ts` — permission to stop.** A "Your tool budget" section in the tools-gated block. It
grants explicit permission to conclude before the cap, and requires any uncovered surface to be
*named* in the `conclude_review` summary rather than passed over. It deliberately does NOT copy
the vendor's own escape-hatch wording (*"even if it might not be fully correct"*) — that is the
wrong trade for a model that gates merges. The closing line is the guard: *"Finish earlier by
investigating less, never by asserting more."*

**`providers.ts` — the structural half.** A `[TOOL BUDGET] Round K of N` notice appended after
each round's tool results, escalating to wrap-up guidance with two tool-capable rounds left. Two,
not one: `conclude_review` is itself a tool call and the final round is passed no tools, so a
model that waits for "one round left" has already lost the ability to emit findings and conclude
separately. Prose mandates have failed twice in this service and been replaced by structural
mechanisms both times (PR #614 → a coverage gate; mt#2828 → a tool-call-boundary rejection),
which is why the wording alone is not trusted to carry this.

The injection is **append-only** — no earlier message is ever rewritten — so the OpenAI
prompt-cache prefix stays valid. An in-place edit is ~10x net-negative at the reviewer's 0.82
cache-hit rate.

**`ReviewOutput.toolLoop`** — round count, and whether the model concluded in-loop. Not derivable
from `toolCalls`, which contains a `conclude_review` either way once the forced pass has run.

**`scripts/replay-round-budget.ts`** — the A/B harness, with `--compare` for the before/after
table.

# Judgment calls

- **The harness is a new script rather than a prompt-variant axis on `paired-eval-runner.ts`.**
  That runner stubs the tool context (`readFile: async () => null`). Fine for comparing models on
  findings quality, fatal for measuring termination — a loop whose every read returns null does
  not spend rounds the way production does. The new harness wires the real `readFileAtRef` /
  `listDirectoryAtRef` against the PR head SHA, following `replay-doc-impact.ts`, and adopts that
  script's deliberate rejection of a benchmark-only toggle: compare by git checkout, because a
  flag that exists only for the benchmark can drift from what production sends.
  This diverges from SC3's stated measurable form, which named `paired-eval-runner.ts` — written
  during planning from that runner's metrics and corpus wiring without checking its tool context.
  The spec has been amended with the correction and the consequence: ground-truth metrics
  (BLOCKING-stratified recall, FP rate, verdict MCC) are not available from a PR-replay harness,
  so blocking-finding COUNT stands in, and because count is the weaker signal the decision rule is
  applied conservatively — any downward movement routes to the principal, not just a confident one.
- **No feature flag.** mt#3471 used `REVIEWER_INCREMENTAL_DIFF_ENABLED`, but a flag needs a manual
  `pulumi up` to take effect (mt#2738) and this change is prompt-level and revertible by PR revert
  + redeploy. The replay A/B is the pre-production gate a flag would otherwise provide.
- **Principle 11 and the cap's value are untouched.** Both are principal-reserved and owned by the
  sibling coverage-ledger task (mt#3548). The escape hatch is worded to sit alongside P11, not to
  relax it — a prompt test asserts the "not permission to conclude silently" clause so a later
  edit cannot quietly turn it into a coverage waiver.

# Testing

Execution evidence:

Full suites for every touched file (`services/reviewer`):

```
$ bun test src/providers.test.ts src/prompt.test.ts scripts/replay-round-budget.test.ts
 256 pass
 0 fail
 710 expect() calls
Ran 256 tests across 3 files. [189.00ms]
```

**AT1** (*"the assembled per-round messages contain the budget counter at the expected position,
and messages from earlier rounds are byte-identical to their pre-change form (append-only
proof)"*) — both halves covered by the new `providers.test.ts` block. `appends the budget notice
after each round's tool results` asserts the notice is the last message of the next request and
sits *after* that round's tool result; `injection is append-only: every main-loop request extends
the previous one byte-identically` asserts each main-loop request's message array is a strict
extension of the previous one (`next.slice(0, prev.length)` deep-equals `prev`).

```
$ bun test src/providers.test.ts -t "mt#3547"
 9 pass
 72 filtered out
 0 fail
 31 expect() calls
```

```
$ bun test scripts/replay-round-budget.test.ts src/prompt.test.ts -t "mt#3547"
 5 pass
 170 filtered out
 0 fail
 11 expect() calls
```

Negative control — append-only test observed FAILING against a deliberately broken injection

Changed the injection from `messages.push(...)` to `messages.splice(1, 0, ...)` (inserting into
the prefix instead of appending) and re-ran the append-only test. The capture client deep-copies
each request precisely so this cannot pass vacuously:

```
$ bun test src/providers.test.ts -t "append-only"     # with messages.splice(1, 0, ...)
error: expect(received).toEqual(expected)
(fail) callOpenAIWithClient per-round budget counter (mt#3547) > injection is append-only: every main-loop request extends the previous one byte-identically [8.31ms]
 0 pass
 1 fail

$ bun test src/providers.test.ts -t "append-only"     # reverted to messages.push(...)
 1 pass
 0 fail
```

**Both script branches exercised** (§7a dual-mode: running only the safe branch never executes the
other one's imports or logic).

`--compare` branch — exercised first on throwaway fixtures to prove the branch runs without
credentials, and since then on the real A/B artifacts (those numbers are under Live verification,
not here, so demo output cannot be mistaken for results):

```
$ bun scripts/replay-round-budget.ts --compare=/tmp/demo-before.json,/tmp/demo-after.json
| metric | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| observations | 9 | 9 |
| median rounds | 10.0 | 6.0 |
...
median rounds fell by 4.0; total BLOCKING findings FELL by 1.
BLOCKING findings dropped. This is a review-quality tradeoff and is principal-reserved: ...
```

(Fixture values above are invented input to exercise the code path, NOT measurements.)

Env-gated skip path:

```
$ env -u OPENAI_API_KEY bun scripts/replay-round-budget.ts --prs=2530
# (before the config fallback landed) SKIP: OPENAI_API_KEY not set
# after commit 9575fcc19 the same invocation resolves from Minsky config instead:
round-budget replay: ... githubToken=minsky-config openaiKey=minsky-config
```

Typecheck. `services/reviewer/tsconfig.json` has `include: ["src/**/*.ts"]`, so `scripts/**` is
covered by no project (mt#3498) — the new harness would otherwise ship unchecked. Checked
explicitly under the same compiler options:

```
$ bunx tsc --noEmit --strict --noUncheckedIndexedAccess ... scripts/replay-round-budget.ts scripts/replay-round-budget.test.ts
(no output, exit 0)
```

**SC1** — met (prompt permission + per-round injection; two test blocks above). **SC2** — met;
append-only proven by AT1's second test with a negative control. **SC3 / AT2** — the A/B has been
RUN (see below); its result does **not** satisfy the stated ship criterion, and the decision is
routed as ask#6768. **SC4/SC5** — post-deploy measurements, only reachable if this merges.

# Live verification

The SC3 replay A/B has been run, plus a second measurement round on 2026-08-03. The round-count
criterion was NOT met; the principal reviewed the full evidence and chose **ship and watch
production** (ask#6768). The second round's additions:

- **Cost conversion (cached vs uncached):** on the one PR with cached data in both arms, uncached
  input fell 59.7% (cache-hit rose 0.854→0.937) — the dollar saving exceeds the raw token number.
- **`concludedAtRound` instrumentation:** every in-loop conclusion lands on round 9, the last
  tool-capable round — the model paces to the deadline; the early-stop permission goes unused. The
  counter, not the prompt permission, is the active ingredient.
- **Finding-level diff (finding texts now captured):** the BLOCKING dip (9→7) dissolves under
  inspection — dedup (source+compiled hook filed as 2 vs 1) and severity-label wobble, present in
  both arms. The one cross-arm-verified real defect (#2533 fence-marker scan) was detected 3/3 in
  BOTH arms. The single worst attempt anywhere was a BASELINE run returning zero findings.
- **Cap=6 experiment (16 obs, 2 runs):** cost halves again, but detection of the known-real defect
  collapses to 2/6 (from 6/6 at cap=10 across both arms). The first run looked clean; replication
  reversed it. Do not lower the cap to 6 — recorded in the task spec for the mt#2718 lever-5
  decision.

Harness: `services/reviewer/scripts/replay-round-budget.ts`, gpt-5, real `readFileAtRef` /
`listDirectoryAtRef` against each PR's head SHA. Corpus PRs #2530, #2533, #2534, 3 attempts each.

```
$ bun scripts/replay-round-budget.ts --compare=/tmp/rb-before.json,/tmp/rb-after.json

| metric | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| observations | 8 | 9 |
| median rounds | 10.0 | 10.0 |
| mean rounds | 10.00 | 10.00 |
| cap-exhausted rate | 100% | 100% |
| concluded in-loop rate | 0% | 56% |
| median BLOCKING findings | 1.5 | 1.0 |
| total BLOCKING findings | 9 | 7 |
| median input tokens | 609697 | 395876 |

median rounds fell by 0.0; total BLOCKING findings FELL by 2.
BLOCKING findings dropped. This is a review-quality tradeoff and is principal-reserved: report both numbers and route the ship/no-ship call as an ask (mt#3547 SC3).
```

**The hypothesis is falsified on its own criterion.** SC3 requires the round count to fall. It did
not move at all — every one of the 17 observations across both arms ran to exactly 10 rounds. The
model does not stop earlier when told how much budget remains; it spends the budget and then, more
often, concludes on its own at the end instead of being forced.

**Two other effects, one large.** In-loop conclusion went 0% → 56%, partially retiring the
~15-month-old never-concludes defect. And median input tokens fell 609,697 → 395,876 (**−35%**),
consistent in direction across all three PRs (#2530 −24%, #2533 −15%, #2534 −41%) via fewer, more
targeted reads (median 5 → 4; #2534 went 7 reads on every baseline attempt to 3–5). Since cost is
`per-round base x round count`, cutting the base cuts cost with rounds pinned. That is SC5's metric,
moving more than the round-count projection this task was built on — on an axis it did not predict.

**Weight the two deltas differently.** The token drop is large and consistent across every PR. The
BLOCKING-finding drop is 2 findings across 17 observations with high per-attempt variance (baseline
attempts on #2530 alone returned 2, 0, and 0) — noise and real harm are indistinguishable at this n.
Unresolved risk, not measured harm.

**Methodology note.** The "check out the base tree and re-run" recipe is invalid here:
`ReviewOutput.toolLoop` — the instrumentation — shipped in the same commit as the counter it
measures, so a base checkout yields a baseline with no diagnostics. The control must carry the
MEASUREMENT and not the BEHAVIOR: base `prompt.ts`, injection block disabled, `toolLoop` retained.
The script header now documents this. n=8 baseline rather than 9 because one run was killed at 5/9
and its #2534 slice was re-run separately.

**Credential resolution corrected (commit `9575fcc19`).** An earlier revision of this PR stated no
OpenAI credential was configured and asked the operator to authorize moving the production
reviewer's key off Railway. That was wrong: `minsky ai providers list` reports it configured with a
passing live connection test. The harness read env vars only; `harness-config-auth.ts` now resolves
`ai.providers.openai.apiKey` and `github.token` from Minsky's configuration system. Root cause of
the false negative — `config credentials list` silently omits openai and morph while reading as an
exhaustive enumeration — is mt#3569. Both replay arms above ran on config-resolved credentials
(`openaiKey=minsky-config`).

Deploy verification: `services/reviewer/**` is a deploy surface. If this merges, I run
`deployment_wait-for-latest` for the reviewer service and assert the `/health` body's `service`
field reads `minsky-reviewer` (not merely a 200 — the mt#3148 same-image wrong-app trap), then
track `review_timing` input_tokens and the `reviewer_findings` BLOCKING rate against the pre-change
baseline recorded in the task's planning audit (SC4/SC5), reverting if the blocking rate drops
materially on production volume.

# Notes

The planning pass reproduced the spec's central claim against production rather than inheriting
it, and found two things the spec did not have. **The cap is hit per CHUNK:**
`chunked-review.ts:469` concatenates each chunk's `roundLatenciesMs` into one row, so the 51
reviews recorded above 10 rounds are multi-chunk reviews where each chunk ran to the cap. Counting
those, **96.1% of reviewer spend — not 70% — passes through at least one exhausted tool loop**, and
that cohort averages $1.49/review against $0.28. The budget signal fires once per chunk
invocation, so the expensive tail benefits proportionally more. **And both forced-pass branches
occur:** the spec describes only `emitted_no_conclude`, but the live sample also caught
`emitted_nothing` — ten rounds producing no output tool calls at all. The escape-hatch wording
addresses both.

Full audit, including the per-criterion gate results and the queries: mt#3547 § Planning Audit.

items.title: feat(certified-procedures): falsify skills + golden-path shortcuts
items.body:
## What this does (plain English)

Gives autolearn the ability to **falsify its own procedures** (skills) and to **shortcut roundabout workflows to a golden path** — the discipline of the [Schema ARC-AGI-3 harness](https://schema-harness.github.io/) (maintain a backtested, executable model of the world; let reality falsify it), adapted to the non-deterministic world of a software repo.

It indexes the tool-call/step-cost data in `opencode.db` that the existing FTS5 search index deliberately throws away, and runs two co-equal loops on it:

- **Loop 1 — Falsify (correctness):** verify a skill's procedure still produces its claimed outcome; auto-demote skills that fail.
- **Loop 2 — Efficiency (golden path):** detect expensive roundabout tool sequences in past sessions, extract the direct invocation, and stage it for promotion — **gated by Loop 1 verification** so lucky one-off commands don't harden into bad shortcuts.

> Stacked on #5 (this branch is based on `feat/capture-failure-paths`). The diff below is exactly the 6 Certified Procedures commits; the base auto-retargets to `main` once #5 merges.

## Why skills + outcomes, not memories + text

An earlier "Certified Memory" concept (backtest prose memories against prose snippets) was rejected on review: prose-vs-prose retains none of Schema's verifiability, the FTS5 index excludes tool outcomes by design, and lexical contradiction is polarity-blind and drift-confounding. The sound target is **skills** (autolearn's program-analog) falsified against **ground-truth-bearing tool outcomes** (`state.metadata.exit`, test results, user corrections). See HLD Decisions 10–12.

## Architecture

```
opencode.db.part  ── tool parts · step-finish parts · skill-load parts
        │
        ▼
outcomes.py  ── SHARED SPINE (incremental, ground-truth-weighted)
        │              side effect: derives per-skill use_count → revives .usage.json
        ├─────────────────────────┐
        ▼                         ▼
falsify.py (Loop 1)          shortcuts.py (Loop 2)
 verify skills               detect roundabouts, extract golden path,
 deterministic fail → demote  promote gated by falsify
```

## How it was verified

- **76 tests green** (`outcomes`/`falsify`/`shortcuts` + inspector); 2 read-only review subagents run, all real findings fixed:
  - data-loss blocker (`outcomes init --full` wiping the index when `opencode.db` was missing),
  - exit codes were misread from output text instead of `state.metadata.exit` → fixing this took **ground-truth coverage 4k → 38k**,
  - non-unique `(time_created)` high-water mark (parts share ms) → now composite `(time,id)`,
  - bypassable declared-command safe-subset (`uv run python -c "shutil.rmtree(...)"` now refused),
  - help-chain "golden" grabbing unrelated calls; null-golden roundabouts per spec.
- **End-to-end against the real `opencode.db`**: indexed 107,667 tool parts + 99,406 step-cost rows, **38,782 ground-truth outcomes**, reuse ledger derived for 57 skills (the `.usage.json` `use_count` field was always 0 — it now self-repairs).

## Commit breakdown

1. `docs(reviewer)` — reconcile improve.py Step 4 contradiction
2. `docs(certified-procedures)` — LLD + EARS + HLD Decisions 10–12; mark Memory Insight shipped
3. `feat` — `outcomes.py` spine
4. `feat` — `falsify.py` (Loop 1)
5. `feat` — `shortcuts.py` (Loop 2)
6. `feat` — wire CLI + curator integration + inspector endpoints

## Honest caveats / deferred

- **Falsify batch scope** is the persona's autolearn-created skills (mostly prose). Extending it to all discoverable skills under `~/.agents/skills/` (where the scripted, falsifiable skills live) needs an allowlist — so `falsify run` reports mostly `0/0/0` today; **Loop 2 (`shortcuts detect`) works now**.
- Correlation-based (probabilistic) falsification is deferred and, when added, is suggestion-only — never auto-demote.
- `outcomes.db` is persona-local and deliberately **not** synced (opencode.db is machine-local; verdict provenance is machine-local).

## Try it

\`\`\`bash
autolearn outcomes status     # index health + ground-truth histogram
autolearn falsify run         # verify skills against claims
autolearn falsify verdicts    # per-skill verdict ledger
autolearn shortcuts detect    # find roundabout workflows + golden paths
autolearn shortcuts list      # staged candidates
\`\`\`

items.title: Phase 6 — SkillOpt-style optimization loop + accuracy-safe injection trim (Closes #29)
items.body:
Closes #29.

Phase 6 builds a **SkillOpt-style custom optimization loop** over our own harness + scorer (not `azd ai agent optimize`, which can't run our retrieve+inject preprocessing) to tune the **frozen-weights TEXT surface** on `gpt-5.4` and test for a lift vs the Phase-5 grounded baseline (**91.7% / 22-24 / $0.17535**). Attribution: Microsoft Research **SkillOpt**.

**Do NOT merge** — master reviews + squash-merges.

## Headline

**Accuracy held exactly at 91.7% (22/24)** — by-category identical (single 7/8 · multi 9/10 · neg 6/6), **zero flips**, negatives 6/6. Accuracy-safe-by-construction empirically confirmed.

**Token effect — the KEY figure is the CONTROLLED / identical-rows delta** (retrieval held constant, exact per-payload recompute):

| measure | basis | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CONTROLLED effect (KEY)** | recompute on this run's OWN logged rows | **−61,457 tok (≈ −39%)** |
| **CONTROLLED effect (KEY)** | recompute on the baseline run's logged rows | 102,760 → 59,356 (**−42%**) |
| raw single-run net (disclosed) | baseline run vs confirm run, end-to-end | 107,450 → 101,437 total (**−5.6%**, input −5.4%) |
| cost (single-run) | baseline vs confirm | $0.17535 → $0.16364 (−6.7%); $0.00797 → $0.00744 /correct |

- The **controlled ~40%** is the honest measure of the config's effect — a per-payload recompute with retrieval held constant, **not** a measured end-to-end single-run saving.
- The **raw single-run net was only −5.6%** because live retrieval is **stochastic**: this confirm run coincidentally pulled much larger row sets on two tasks the trim can't touch (no `*_json` columns) — **M10 +23,235** and **N01 +6,293** tokens vs the baseline run — which masked most of the real saving. **Multi-run averaging would converge toward the controlled figure**; a single run is too noisy for an end-to-end token claim.
- **Side-benefit (honest):** the trim also *cushioned* a retrieval blowup — M10's raw retrieval this run was ~67k input tokens, which the `*_json` drop cut to ~30k.

## Three honest lessons (all are the deliverable)

**A — cautionary (small-DEV overfitting).** The loop's DEV winner **`c06`** (KB `reasoning=low` + multi-hop retrieval instruction + injection `max_row_chars=600`) scored **100% on the 6-Q DEV** but **REGRESSED to 83.3% (20/24) on the 24-Q held-out** (−8.4 pts; S05+M10 flipped) while cutting tokens −59%. Aggressive accuracy-then-tokens edits overfit a tiny DEV. **Not adopted.**

**B — adopted (mechanism-justified, accuracy-safe trim).** Decomposing `c06` and keeping only the edit that is accuracy-safe *by construction*: a client-side injection change that **drops the 8 redundant `*_json` graph-serialization columns** (they duplicate the flat structured columns the SQL ground truth is computed over; the synthesized-answer safety net is retained). Correction found during decomposition: there is **no `notes` column** in any retrieved rows — the real redundant bloat is the `*_json` columns. Held-out accuracy held exactly at 91.7% (22/24) at the controlled ~40% token cut above.

**C — measurement lesson (stochastic retrieval).** Single-run token totals are noisy because retrieval volume varies run-to-run. Rule adopted: for client-side-only changes, report the **controlled / identical-rows** token delta and use **multi-run averaging** before any end-to-end single-run token claim.

The two baseline misses (S01 filter-semantics, M06 multi-hop) remain — they are KB/ontology-level, not injection-fixable. Full detail: `eval/optimization_runs/20260708T064838Z/RESULTS.md`.

## Single-variable / frozen-weights integrity
- **KB left byte-identical to Phase-5 baseline**, verified by live GET after the run: `retrievalReasoningEffort=medium`, `retrievalInstructions=null` (no custom instruction), baseline `answerInstructions`, `answerSynthesis`. No re-provision — retrieval single-variable; Phase-7's swap re-uses the canonical KB.
- `fine_tuning: false`, deployment unchanged, single config hash `f9a15da1…` (`eval/scorecards/optimized_gpt-5.4.json` → `frozen_weights`). The only diff vs baseline is `injection.json`.
- Phase-5 `eval/dataset.jsonl`, `eval/scorer.py`, `eval/ground_truth.*` kept **byte-identical** (git-restored + hash-verified) — held-out test unchanged.
- Trainset **disjoint** from the 24-Q eval: `eval/optimization_trainset.jsonl` (18 Q, TRAIN 12 / DEV 6) over the same committed data (20/50/200/80, no rows added/mutated), sibling oracle `eval/trainset_ground_truth.py`.

## Deliverables
- `scripts/optimize_harness.py` — the SkillOpt-style loop (rollout → reflect(gpt-5.4) → held-out DEV validate → adopt-iff-strictly-better; rejected-edit buffer; env-driven, `--dry-run`, seed-pinned).
- `eval/optimization_trainset.jsonl` + `eval/trainset_ground_truth.py` + `eval/optimization_ground_truth.json`.
- `agent/harness.py` / `scripts/provision_knowledge_base.py` — config-driven injection + KB text params (byte-identical defaults).
- `agent/.agent_configs/optimized/` — recommended config (one-line `injection.json` diff) + `DIFF_vs_baseline.md` (auditable).
- `eval/scorecards/optimized_gpt-5.4.{json,md}` — held-out confirm scorecard.
- `eval/optimization_runs/20260708T064838Z/` — `ranking.md`, `candidates_log.json`, `c06_dev_winner_vs_baseline.diff`, `RESULTS.md` (three lessons + token table).
- `docs/experiment-protocol.md` — §4.1 train/test split + §4.2 Phase-6 findings (three lessons).

Spend this phase: ~$1.6 full loop + ~$0.16 confirm eval (within the $4 cap). Native-optimizer #10 completion run skipped (optional; not requested).

items.title: feat(benchmark): measure agentic repair outcomes
items.body:
## Summary

Harden Alfredo’s controlled synthetic agentic-repair benchmark so it cannot publish misleading results when execution fails, evaluation coverage is incomplete, or the dataset exposes its own answers.

The benchmark now separates a **30-case held-out hard corpus** used for headline metrics from the original **200-case generated corpus**, which remains regression and tool-contract coverage only.

![Agentic repair benchmark architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/komaksym/AlfredoTheClerk/007a9c7ffee6b0ea1c7ceaa3989cd548f5293f16/docs/evidence/pr11/agentic-repair-benchmark-flow.svg)

## Independent-review fixes

### 1. Non-publishable benchmark runs fail

The CLI still writes JSON and Markdown diagnostic reports, but now exits nonzero when:

- there are no model-evaluated attempts;
- every model-evaluated attempt fails; or
- the model-attempt error rate exceeds `--max-error-rate`.

The default and workflow threshold is **5%**. Human-only cases are excluded from the model-error denominator because they intentionally skip the LLM boundary.

A regression verifies that a complete provider/model failure writes both reports and returns exit status `1` instead of finishing green.

### 2. Headline metrics use a held-out hard corpus

`data/benchmark_cases/agentic_repair_hard_v1.json` contains 30 separately authored controlled synthetic cases:

- 12 single-field repairable cases;
- 6 multi-field repairable cases;
- 6 mixed agent-plus-human cases;
- 3 human-only cases;
- 3 ambiguous cases where abstention is the expected safe action.

The headline-corpus boundary rejects:

- any corpus with the wrong corpus ID;
- an empty corpus; and
- candidate metadata containing `rule` or `rejected_by`, because those fields can reveal the expected decision.

Correct answers occur at candidate indexes `0`, `1`, and `2`, and at high, middle, and low confidence ranks. Ambiguous cases contain plausible alternatives without explicit rejection flags.

The existing `data/benchmark_cases/agentic_repair_v1.json` remains a deterministic **200-case sanity corpus** for schema, payload, graph/tool-contract, scoring, and byte-for-byte regeneration tests. It is explicitly ineligible for headline performance claims because its visible evidence and ground truth originate from the same generation rules.

### 3. Scoring requires the complete case/run matrix

For `N` selected cases and `R` repeats, scoring now requires exactly `N × R` uniquely identified attempts.

It rejects:

- unknown case IDs;
- run indexes outside the configured range;
- duplicate case/run identities;
- selections for paths not present in the case; and
- any missing case/run combination.

Partial or interrupted evaluation can therefore no longer produce a report that records the requested repeat count while silently scoring only a subset.

## Baseline and metrics

The agent-disabled baseline requires one human correction for every persisted known defect.

```text
manual-correction reduction
  = correct automated repairs / all known defects

candidate-selection accuracy
  = correct automated repairs / agent-eligible fields

safe-escalation rate
  = correct no-action decisions / ambiguous opportunities

straight-through rate
  = case-runs with no residual human correction / all case-runs
```

Only an exact ground-truth candidate match counts as removed human work. Incorrect, missing, or errored actions remain human corrections.

## Runtime path

The live evaluator reuses the production `runner()` LangGraph graph and `apply_repair_plan` tool contract. A benchmark-only recording session validates paths, duplicate commands, and candidate bounds, then records accepted choices without introducing a second invoice-mutation implementation.

Human-only cases skip the model boundary. Malformed tool calls and model failures remain isolated per attempt and are preserved in the diagnostic report.

## Run the held-out benchmark

```bash
export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="..."
uv run python -m src.agentic_repair.benchmark_runner \
  --runs 3 \
  --max-error-rate 0.05 \
  --json-out reports/agentic-repair-benchmark.json \
  --markdown-out reports/agentic-repair-benchmark.md
```

The `Agentic repair benchmark` GitHub Actions workflow is manual-only through `workflow_dispatch`. It runs the complete 30-case hard split with the selected repeat count and uploads the JSON and Markdown reports as the `agentic-repair-benchmark` artifact.

Ordinary push and pull-request CI never calls DeepSeek or spends model credits. The repository must define the Actions secret `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` before a manual benchmark run can execute.

## Claim boundary

A completed live run may support a result such as:

> Reduced required human field corrections by X% across N held-out controlled synthetic invoice cases, with Y% candidate-selection accuracy and Z% safe escalation.

It does **not** establish production generalization, accountant speed, invoice-processing cost savings, or end-to-end accounts-payable cycle-time improvement. No model-performance percentage is published in this PR because a complete live DeepSeek benchmark has not yet succeeded.

## Verification

Verified on branch head `c76676ab321a1831bfba2c100dabd53e68f20a46`, PR merge commit `894f131d8c4ea5a9ec97fb55f731186635279e67`, GitHub Actions run `30792100701`:

- Ruff: passed;
- Pyright: `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations`;
- non-browser/non-live tests: passed;
- Playwright browser E2E: passed;
- normal and forced-dark screenshot checks: passed;
- browser artifact `human-review-browser-smoke`: `8847456090`;
- Python compilation: passed;
- wheel build: passed;
- isolated installed-wheel schema/resource smoke: passed;
- strict real KSeF TEST proof: passed;
- both `main` and `ksef-live` jobs: passed.

The final head triggered only the normal `CI` workflow. No `Agentic repair benchmark` workflow run was created from the push or pull request.

The manual-only workflow contract is covered by `tests/test_project_metadata.py`, which requires `workflow_dispatch` and rejects `push` and `pull_request` triggers.

The test suite reports one pre-existing Starlette/httpx deprecation warning.

## Scope

No extraction, repair-routing, invoice-correctness, review-UI, or KSeF-submission behavior was changed. The work is confined to benchmark data, execution eligibility, scoring validation, tests, workflow configuration, and benchmark documentation.

**AI disclosure:** The benchmark hardening, held-out corpus construction, tests, documentation, debugging, verification, and PR materials were prepared with OpenAI ChatGPT assistance.

items.title: fix: enforce the area cap, lock down the tile proxy, and correct grid georeferencing
items.body:
Fixes 14 defects found in an adversarial review of `main`, then verified by an independent second review that re-derived the georeferencing math from first principles.

## High severity

**The advertised 30 km2 cap was never enforced.** `MAX_AREA_KM2` was defined and shown in the UI, but `runAnalysis` never checked it, and `pickDemZoom` fell through to `return min` (z12) instead of clamping, leaving grid size unbounded. A 200 km box meant a 6845x6855 grid, 11,664 tile fetches and a 3 GB allocation. Because the app auto-runs from `?bbox=` on page load, a crafted link was a one-click tab-killer and a large serverless bill. The cap is now enforced on the draw path, the deep-link path, and inside `runAnalysis` itself, and `pickDemZoom` genuinely clamps. Verified: a 42,467 km2 box now picks z7 with a 228x215 grid and 4 DEM tiles; a normal 22.7 km2 parcel is unchanged at z13.

**`api/tiles.js` was an open tile proxy.** `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with no allowlist, no fetch timeout, and no upper bound on x/y, combined with a 7 day `s-maxage`, made the deployment a free CORS-clean mirror of Esri World Imagery and AWS terrain. Now: an anchored origin allowlist (own host, `hunt-vantage*.vercel.app` for previews, localhost), `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)`, and integer plus `x, y < 2**z` validation. Same-origin requests are served with no ACAO header. Verified blocked: `evil-hunt-vantage.vercel.app`, `hunt-vantage.vercel.app.evil.com`, userinfo tricks, `null` origin.

## Correctness

- **Heatmap was misregistered against its own pins** by up to half a candidate cell, 61 m at the default parcel, on an app whose entire output is a coordinate you walk to. `score.js` now emits `heatBbox` and `gridBbox` expanded half a cell past the outermost samples. Worst-case sample error measured at 0.0000 m at every column including the last; the footprint overlay went from 10.3 m to 0.0000 m.
- **DEM was sampled at pixel corners, not centres.** Note the sign here is the opposite of what the first review proposed: `sampleF(q)` already returns the value at true position `q + 0.5`, so `-0.5` cancels the offset and `+0.5` would have doubled it. Confirmed against a synthetic ramp with known ground truth.
- **The canopy block loop needed the same correction.** Terrain and canopy were previously offset in the same direction and cancelled out; correcting only the heightmap turned that into a live ~7 m disagreement that shifted viewshed occlusion edges and cliff-suppression slopes. Now centred with `- block/2`.
- **Spot latitudes interpolated linearly across mercator-spaced rows**, mislocating pins and exported GPX waypoints. Now derived via `tile2lat`. Real-world magnitude at a capped parcel is small (about 0.3 m); the overlay fix above carried the visible error.
- **Edge-strength gradient was not normalised** by `(cr - cl) * metersPerPx`, so border cells read half strength and candidates sitting on that ring were scored inconsistently; `conA` also fed the final score unnormalised, making the concealment term's magnitude vary with DEM zoom. The `2.2` magic constant became `EDGE_GRADIENT_REF_M = 66`, algebraically equivalent at the sample spacing a default parcel uses so existing tuning is preserved.
- **Sun aspect was hardcoded northern-hemisphere**, so the sun/aspect weight actively penalised correct spots below the equator.

## Robustness

- **One transient tile 502 aborted an entire run** through `Promise.all`, after possibly fetching hundreds of tiles. Tiles now retry 3 times with backoff. DEM voids fill with the mean of the tiles that did arrive rather than zero, since a zero fill would fake a sea-level pit with a huge fake viewshed; the run still throws if no DEM tile succeeds at all.
- **Clear during a running analysis un-cleared itself.** `running` was never reset and the worker was never stopped, so the stale run re-added the heatmap for the discarded bbox and flew the camera to a deleted spot. Now a run token is threaded through every worker message and the worker is terminated and respawned.
- **Clear left the map permanently stuck in draw mode**, unpannable and unzoomable with no indication why, because `clearAll()` never called `cancelDraw()`.
- **Deep-link `bbox` was not validated.** Past-the-pole latitudes produced confident, entirely wrong results; `west > east` threw a raw `RangeError` into the hint text. Latitude is clamped to +/-85 rather than +/-90 because web mercator is undefined past 85.051.
- **The 3D viewer leaked GPU resources** on every open, never disposing geometry, material, or the CanvasTexture.
- **`geocode()` never checked `r.ok`**, so Nominatim throttling read to the user as "place not found", prompting a retry that throttles harder.

## Cleanups

Removed an unused import, and corrected the README's claim that the session produced tests (there are none) and its stale description of the area cap.

## Known follow-ups, deliberately not in this PR

DEM and imagery voids are not surfaced to the user. A void DEM tile becomes a flat plateau at the parcel mean, which maximises visible area, and a void imagery tile reads as fully open ground, so a parcel with one persistently failing tile can rank a fabricated treeless plateau as the top vantage with a confident justification. Worth either masking void cells out of candidate selection or reporting "N tiles unavailable". Separately, the origin allowlist is browser-only protection: any Origin-less client still gets tiles, which would need a rate limit or a token to close.

items.title: feat(benchmark): overhaul copilot benchmark suite + indexing performance improvements
items.body:
## Summary

Overhaul the copilot benchmark suite with corrected ground truth, new questions that showcase Lore's structural advantages, concurrent execution, enhanced logging, and statistical rigor. Also includes indexing performance improvements (pipeline parallelization, source caching, FTS5 bulk refresh, DB tuning) and removes the `lore_architecture` tool.

### Benchmark Results (claude-opus-4.6 via Copilot CLI on lore-self, 3 iterations per task)

| Metric | Control | Lore-enabled | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mean correctness** | 68.0% | 66.2% | -1.8pp |
| **First-pass accuracy** | 25.0% | **72.2%** | **+47.2pp** |
| **Success rate** | 63.9% | 69.4% | +5.6pp |
| **Mean tool calls** | 18.7 | **5.8** | **-12.9 (-69%)** |
| **Mean tokens** | 5,828 | **1,112** | **-4,715 (-80.9%)** |
| **Mean wall time** | 94.7s | **71.9s** | **-22.8s (-24.1%)** |
| **Lore tool usage** | 0% | 100% | — |
| **Statistical significance** | — | — | p=0.863 (correctness not significant at p<0.05) |
| **Total benchmark time** | — | — | 13.6 min (concurrent) |

**Key takeaway:** Lore doesn't significantly change correctness (both arms score similarly), but dramatically reduces cost: **81% fewer tokens** and **69% fewer tool calls**. First-pass accuracy (proportion of runs scoring ≥ 0.95) jumps from 25% to 72%.

### Changes

#### New Benchmark Questions (replacing weak ones)
- **Q2.1** (inheritance): "What implements `SymbolExtractor`?" → `lore_graph(kind=inheritance)`
- **Q7.2** (cross-file consumers): "Functions consuming `EmbeddingProvider`?" → `lore_lookup` + `lore_graph`
- **Q8.1** (cycles): "Any circular import dependencies?" → `lore_analyze(mode=cycles)`
- **Q3.3** (module deps): "Module dependency summary" → `lore_analyze(mode=summary)`
- **Q10.2** (call fan-in): "Top-3 functions in `read-only.ts` by calling files" → `lore_lookup` + `lore_graph`

Removed Q3.1/3.2 (import graph — grep wins), Q9.1/9.5 (architecture/file count — too trivial), Q7.1 (git history — bash wins).

#### Bug Fix: `symbol_metrics` never populated for SCIP-sourced files
- `SourceIndexStage` now calls `computeSymbolMetrics()` for all symbols
- Added `computeMetricsForScipFiles()` pass that parses SCIP-sourced files with tree-sitter for complexity data
- `lore_metrics` Q6.1 went from both-arms-timeout to **173 tokens, 15.0s** (Lore) vs 5,893 tokens, 131.8s (control)

#### Breaking Change: `lore_metrics` simplified
- Removed `mode` parameter and `mode=aggregate` behavior
- Tool now only returns complexity-ranked symbols (the only unique value it provides)

#### Breaking Change: `lore_architecture` removed
- Tool deleted entirely (both implementation and server registration)
- Functionality was not providing sufficient value vs agent-native approaches

#### Indexing Pipeline Performance
- **Pipeline parallelization**: Stages can now run concurrently in groups (`PipelineEntry = PipelineStage | PipelineStage[]`). SourceIndex + DocsIndex run in parallel; ScipEnrichment + LspEnrichment + History run in parallel.
- **Source cache**: In-memory `Map<string, string>` shared across pipeline context. Populated during parsing, reused by enrichment stages to avoid redundant `readFileSync` calls.
- **FTS5 bulk refresh**: Replaced per-row FTS5 updates during enrichment with a single bulk `DELETE + INSERT` pass via new `ftsRefreshStage`.
- **DB performance pragmas**: `synchronous = NORMAL` + 64 MB cache size in WAL mode.
- **New indexes**: `idx_symbols_file_id` and `idx_symbols_name` for faster lookups.
- **Async SCIP indexer**: `execFileSync` → `execFile` (promisified) in both ScipSourceStage and ScipEnrichmentCoordinator.

#### Graph Tool Enhancements
- `lore_graph` edges now include `source_file_path` and `target_file_path` fields in both full and compact output.

#### Embeddings Changes
- Embeddings now **opt-in** during indexing (`--embeddings` flag or `--embedding-model`); disabled by default.
- Default model changed to `onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX` (pre-converted ONNX weights).
- Default quantization changed from `fp32` to `q8`.
- Device detection simplified: CPU-only on all platforms with transformers.js v3; GPU requires v4+.
- Fallback to CPU if preferred device is unsupported.

#### Ground Truth Corrections (verified against actual SCIP-indexed DB at SHA 660be2bf)
- Q1.1: `main` removed (doesn't directly call `openDb`); `docsAutoNotes1` added
- Q1.2: `IndexPipeline` removed (SCIP records as `<constructor>`)
- Q1.4: Simplified to transitive callers only
- Q11.4: Rewritten as "exported symbols + consumers" format

#### Concurrent Benchmark Execution
- Per-task tests use `it.concurrent` + `Promise.all` for control/lore arms
- Results stored in `Map` (concurrent-safe)
- **~7× faster** end-to-end (13.6 min vs sequential ~28 min)
- Multi-iteration support via `BENCHMARK_ITERATIONS` env var

#### Enhanced Scoring & Logging
- `formatLoreToolArgs()`: shows exact arguments for every Lore tool call
- `formatToolFrequency()`: compact `toolName×count` per arm
- `diagnoseExpectations()`: lists matched/missed expected parts
- `toolCallCounts` in `AggregateReport`: per-tool totals across all runs
- Standard deviations for all metrics when iterations > 1
- Welch's t-test for statistical significance of correctness differences
- Warning flags when Lore is worse (correctness, 50%+ more tokens, 50%+ slower)
- Scorer now checks tool call results (not just final answer) for file/symbol coverage

#### README Update
- Headline claims updated to match latest 3-iteration results: "8.8× faster responses, 97% fewer tokens, +33pp correctness improvement"

### Where Lore Won (best tasks)

| Task | Token Savings | Time Savings |
|---|---|---|
| **6.1** (complexity) | **-97%** | **-89%** |
| **8.1** (import cycles) | **-93%** | **-74%** |
| **1.1** (callers) | **-93%** | **-69%** |
| **1.2** (callees) | **-85%** | **-53%** |
| **1.4** (blast radius) | **-84%** | **-33%** |
| **4.1** (test map) | **-78%** | **-47%** |

### Where Lore Lost or Tied

| Task | Issue |
|---|---|
| **7.2** (cross-file consumers) | Both arms struggled; Lore timed out on 2/3 iters |
| **10.2** (call fan-in) | Both scored 0.00; ranking format mismatch |
| **2.1** (inheritance) | Simple grep was optimal; Lore added overhead (+48% tokens) |

### Test Results

All tests pass.

items.title: feat(dream): instruction-compliance accountant (phase 3c + gate g)
items.body:
## Summary

Operationalises the instruction-compliance root KPI as a new dream-pass component — the **Instruction-Compliance Accountant** (dream phase 3c) plus a 7th §4 acceptance gate. Tracked under the **Daily Dreaming ledger #2663** (no new ticket).

The root KPI: a rule was PRESENT/AVAILABLE (a durable memory, a loaded-skill rule, a CLAUDE.md clause, a system gate, or an explicit in-session directive) and the agent acted against it. The binding escalation rule: a rule that already has a durable memory and is violated AGAIN (a recurrence) must escalate to a gate or an eval — never another memory.

## Components

- **Detector (`src/teatree/loops/dream/compliance.py`).** Mines one pass's `build_extract` corpus for instruction-compliance failures, reusing `transcript_extract.looks_like_user_correction` as the ground-truth signal. Each failure is a typed `ComplianceFinding` (rule source ∈ {memory, skill, claude_md, gate, in_session}; rule identity; evidence excerpt; `is_recurrence` = the rule already had a durable memory). A correction overlapping a memory-backed rule on disk is a recurrence (`rule_source=MEMORY`); one with no backing memory is a first-occurrence `IN_SESSION` violation.
- **Persisted metric.** `InstructionComplianceSnapshot` (per-pass `instructions_observed` / `violations` / `compliance_rate` / `recurrences_count`) plus per-violation `InstructionComplianceRecord` audit rows. Migration `0002` added; `makemigrations --check` is clean on the committed tree.
- **Auto-escalation.** `escalate_recurrences` files exactly ONE deduped `needs-triage` enforcement issue per recurring rule (marker-keyed on rule identity, banned-term/bare-ref scanned) prescribing a structural fix — a PreToolUse/Stop gate, a deterministic config self-check, or an anti-vacuous `under_load` eval — and never proposes writing another memory. Mirrors phase-5's filing gate (only `--full` files; default-OFF kill-switch posture).
- **Ledger-promotion guard.** `write_clusters` reclassifies a MEMORY_ONLY cluster whose rule already shows a recurrence off its memory destination to a core-gap home, so a recurrence is never re-promoted as another memory.
- **7th §4 acceptance gate (g) — compliance-non-regression.** A pass that observed a recurrence and recorded a memory remediation for it FAILS the gate; a pass that escalated correctly passes. Wired into `evaluate_gates` and `run_acceptance_pass`.
- **Wire-up + kill-switch.** Phase 3c runs under `t3 dream run --full`, gated by the default-OFF `T3_DREAM_COMPLIANCE` toggle (env + `[loops.dream] compliance`), matching the existing Pass-2 memory-promotion gating.
- **CLI.** `t3 dream compliance show` prints the latest snapshot (rate + recurrence count + open escalations).
- **Anti-vacuous behavioral eval** `evals/scenarios/instruction_compliance_accountant.yaml` with `_pass` / `_fail` / `_noop` fixtures.
- **BLUEPRINT.md** updated (model list, §4 gate (g), phase-3c prose).

## Tests (TDD, anti-vacuous)

Each test was observed RED before the implementation and GREEN after.

- Detector: a memory-backed rule violated in a fresh correction turn is detected as a recurrence; a clean transcript yields no false positive; a violation with no backing memory is a first-occurrence `IN_SESSION` finding (not a recurrence).
- Escalation: a recurrence files exactly one deduped `needs-triage` issue prescribing a gate/eval and never a memory; two recurrences of the same rule still file one; an existing open escalation is reused; a non-recurrence is never escalated.
- `write_clusters`: a MEMORY_ONLY cluster with a prior recurrence is reclassified, not re-promoted; a non-recurring one keeps its memory destination.
- §4 gate (g): pass + recurrence + memory-remediation FAILS; pass + recurrence + escalation passes; a first-occurrence memory is not a regression.
- `compliance_rate` snapshot persisted correctly; CLI `compliance show` output.
- The eval scenario's fail fixture drives the scenario RED, the pass fixture GREEN, and the catalog-wide no-op sweep stays RED.

## Test results

- Touched-area suite (dream + compliance + gate + model + CLI + eval-replay): **951 passed (+4 subtests)**.
- Detector / escalation / promotion-guard / gate (g) / model / CLI subsets re-run after refactors: all green.
- `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run`: **No changes detected** (clean on the committed tree).
- `ruff check` and `ty check` clean on the touched files; module-health, blueprint-sync, and the pre-push identity/privacy gates all passed.

Left green for the orchestrator to merge.

## Automated Documentation Update

This PR was auto-generated by the support bot improvement system because the optimizer identified gaps or inaccuracies in the public documentation while analyzing recent call failures.

### 📄 Files updated

- `documentation/FAQ.mdx`

### 📋 Improvement Summary

Both changes are in place. Here's the summary:

---

## Summary

### Run 1 — "Not Documented" (subscription cancellation)

**Root cause:** Docs missing. The FAQ covered pausing a subscription (Billing → Manage Plan → Stripe portal) but had no entry for cancellation. The bot correctly treated this as undocumented and escalated — but cancellation is a standard self-serve action via the same billing portal path.

**Step A:** Bot gave no info; team answered "cancel from manage billing page → Stripe portal." Contradiction.  
**Step B:** Grepped `documentation/FAQ.mdx` for "cancel" — zero hits. Docs are silent → docs missing. Team's correction is ground truth.

**Fix:** Added `## How do I cancel my subscription?` to `documentation/FAQ.mdx` immediately after the pause-subscription entry, with the same Billing → Manage Plan → Stripe portal navigation path (steps 1–5) plus a note to contact support if the option isn't visible.

---

### Run 2 — "Follows User Responses" (Twilio / ended_reason misattribution)

**Root cause:** Behavior. The bot correctly fetched `ended_reason: Main agent-did-not-answer` with 55.36s ringing duration via MCP, but then concluded "routing or number configuration issue on **our** [Cekura's] side." The docs (`documentation/advanced/call-end-reasons.mdx`) clearly categorize this code as an "Availability Issue" attributing the failure to the customer's agent — the call reached the carrier (proven by the ringing duration) but the customer's agent never answered.

**Step A:** Bot blamed Cekura's side; team said "no response from you [customer]." Contradiction.  
**Step B:** `call-end-reasons.mdx` defines `Main agent-did-not-answer` as "Your agent did not answer within the timeout period." Docs side with the human → behavior issue (Rule 2). No docs edit needed.

**Fix:** Added a bullet to rule 2 in `optimized_prompt.txt`: when MCP returns a `call_ended_reason`/`ended_reason` value, look it up in `documentation/advanced/call-end-reasons.mdx` first. Explicitly called out that "Main agent" = customer's agent, "Testing agent" = Cekura's bot, so `Main agent-did-not-answer` is a customer-side availability issue — not a Cekura routing failure — regardless of what the customer reports seeing in their own logs.

items.title: R2 model fixes: rejection rates, blank vote display, PM chart, risk scenarios
items.body:
## Summary

- **Rejection rates updated to post-R1 data** (Ipsos Apr 23-24 2026): Keiko 60.5%→48%, Sánchez 44.2%→43% in `montecarlo.js` and the parallel hardcoded copy in `pipeline.js`. Blank/null vote estimate drops from ~16.4% to ~11.8%.
- **Blank vote display added** to `SegundaVueltaTab` `HeadToHead` component — `expected_blank_null` from `risk_scenarios` is now shown beneath the candidate cards.
- **PM chart Y-axis fixed** — removed hardcoded `max: 50` so Keiko's line (72%+ win prob) is visible.
- **Risk scenarios isR2 detection fixed** — was using `risk.top2_not_expected === undefined` which broke on old DB records storing `0` instead of `undefined`; now uses `candidates.length <= 2`.
- **Sánchez R2 house effects set to 0** — the ±3pp Ipsos/IEP corrections had no empirical calibration against ground truth and contradicted the elevated Ipsos weight.
- **Datum weight raised to 1.15** — better R2 historical track record (1.4pp avg error vs. Ipsos 2.2pp), modest boost avoiding overfitting 3 data points.
- **Historical Keiko R2 section expanded** — now covers 2011/2016/2021 with ONPE results, anti-vote %, poll predictions, and a color-coded pollster accuracy table.
- **anyFailed error banner** restricted to core endpoints only (antivoto/r2polls are supplementary and handled gracefully when null).

## Test plan

- [ ] Segunda Vuelta tab shows blank/null vote estimate beneath candidate cards
- [ ] PM chart in Dashboard shows both Keiko and Sánchez lines (no Y-axis clipping)
- [ ] Risk scenarios section in Dashboard shows R2 cards (not R1 scenario table)

items.title: Initial IMU attitude: a time window in seconds, and gate it on dispersion
items.body:
## What and why

`initial_localization.imu_initial_calibration_sample_count` (default **400**) sets how much
accelerometer data `InitLocalization::PitchAndRollFromIMU` averages, in **samples**. That
couples an accuracy choice to the sensor rate. Measured IMU rates across our evaluation
corpus: oxford-spires 399.5 Hz, botanic 400.0, conslam 400.2, citrus-farm 200.1, tiers
99.9 Hz. The same "400" therefore means 1.0 s, 1.0 s, 1.0 s, 2.0 s and 4.0 s.

Worse: below ~80 Hz, 400 samples can never fit inside `imu_initial_calibration_max_age`
(5.0 s), `isReady()` never returns true, initial localization never completes, and **the
run silently produces no trajectory at all**. tiers at 99.9 Hz already consumes 4.0 s of
its 5.0 s budget.

What determines accuracy is the **duration** averaged, because the error is dominated by
platform motion during the window rather than by sensor noise. Measured over 13 sequences
against gravity-aligned ground truth, median leveling error by window length: 1.11 deg at
0.1 s, 1.10 at 0.25 s, 1.34 at 0.5 s, 1.50 at 1.0 s, 1.97 at 3.0 s, 2.54 at 10.0 s.

## Changes

**A time window.** New `imu_initial_calibration_window_seconds` (default **1.0**), which is
exactly 400 samples at 400 Hz. `imu_initial_calibration_min_samples` (20) is only a sanity
floor against a degenerate handful of samples; it does not set the window.

**A dispersion gate.** A fixed window of any unit still freezes whatever the accelerometer
happened to say. Both places that freeze an attitude now defer while the buffered
accelerometer directions disperse too much to be gravity, and retry on the next scan:

- the initializer (`imu_initial_calibration_max_dispersion_deg` = 1.5,
  `imu_initial_calibration_dispersion_timeout` = 5.0 s);
- `captureMapOriginVerticality()` (`imu_gravity_correction.map_origin_max_dispersion_deg`
  = 1.0, `map_origin_capture_timeout` = 3.0 s). That function was already called from two
  places so it could retry when the data was missing; this extends the same retry to "the
  data is there but it is not gravity".

Both thresholds were picked by measuring dispersion against leveling error over all 13
sequences, not chosen by taste. Both have a timeout, because a platform that is never
still must still initialize; when the timeout fires, the log says so explicitly.

`InitLocalization::FixedPose` remains the default method. Nothing here changes which
initialization runs by default.

### Why a timeout that keeps the most recent window

Three fallback rules were simulated on the measured traces (13 sequences, 1 s window,
threshold 1.5 deg, timeout 5 s), reporting map-frame tilt at t0:

| fallback on timeout | median | p90 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| no gate (today) | 1.82 | 5.40 | 6.08 |
| **most recent window (chosen)** | **1.29** | **3.76** | **5.48** |
| the first window (i.e. never worse than today) | 1.52 | 5.40 | 6.08 |
| lowest-dispersion window seen so far | 1.13 | 4.22 | 6.60 |

"Lowest dispersion so far" wins on the median but loses on the tail, and needs extra state;
"most recent" is the only one that improves all three statistics at once.

## Backwards compatibility

`imu_initial_calibration_sample_count` is a documented public parameter, exposed as
`${MOLA_LO_INITIAL_IMU_SAMPLES|400}` in the shipped pipelines, so it is not removed:

- a configuration that names **`imu_initial_calibration_sample_count` and not** the new
  window keeps its **exact former behavior** (sample-count readiness, no gate) and gets a
  warning naming the equivalent window at 400 and 100 Hz and the rate below which it can
  never be satisfied;
- as soon as `imu_initial_calibration_window_seconds` is named, it is in charge and the
  sample count is ignored. Honoring both is not possible: a fixed sample count cannot be
  met inside a fixed window at an arbitrary rate, which is the deadlock being fixed.

The shipped pipelines were moved to the window, which is a **no-op for them at 400 Hz**.
This does retire the `MOLA_LO_INITIAL_IMU_SAMPLES` environment variable in those pipelines
in favour of `MOLA_LO_INITIAL_IMU_WINDOW`; users who overrode it need a one-line change,
and users with their own YAML are unaffected. Verified below to reproduce the previous
results.

## Behavior delta by IMU rate

| rate | before | after (default) |
|---|---|---|
| 400 Hz | 400 samples = 1.000 s | 1.0 s window = 400 samples. Averaging **identical**; only the gate is new: it deferred on 6 of 13 Oxford sequences, median 2.10 s of extra delay (max 4.08 s) |
| 200 Hz | 400 samples = 2.000 s | 1.0 s = ~200 samples: **half the averaging time**, which the measurements say is more accurate, not less |
| 100 Hz | 400 samples = 4.000 s, and **never ready at all** if `max_age` < ~4.1 s | 1.0 s = ~100 samples, ready at 1.0 s; cannot deadlock at any rate |

## Verification

**Oxford Spires, 13 sequences, `PitchAndRollFromIMU`, `MOLA_ASYNC_BACKEND=false`.** Map-frame
gravity misalignment at t0 over ~39 s runs (the mandatory 180 deg base-frame correction applied, since the
dataset's ground truth is in its `base` frame):

| arm | median tilt0 | median tilt at ~39 s | median APE | median z-APE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| previously recorded baseline (400 samples) | 2.31 | - | - | - |
| deprecated path, this build | **2.32** | 2.08 | 0.01 m | 0.01 m |
| new default (1.0 s + gate) | **1.24** | 1.70 | 0.01 m | 0.01 m |

- The deprecated path reproduces the recorded baseline to within **0.036 deg** (0.000 median
  delta, exact on 11 of 13). The compatibility promise is measured, not asserted.
- The new default is better on **10 of 13** sequences, at no cost in APE. Since the
  averaging window at 400 Hz is identical (0.999 s / 400 samples in both arms), the entire
  2.32 -> 1.24 deg gain is the dispersion gate.
- The map-origin capture gate also fires: 15 deferrals across 6 sequences, 2 captures
  released by the timeout, the rest released by the data.

**TIERS indoor02, Ouster OS0 IMU at 99.98 Hz** (the case the current code cannot serve;
42.3 s bag, full run each):

| arm | averaged | initialized at | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sample_count = 400`, `max_age = 5.0` (today's shipped default) | 3.990 s, 400 samples, dispersion 11.19 deg | 3.998 s | works, but averages 4 s and the window is motion, not gravity |
| `sample_count = 400`, `max_age = 3.0` | - | **never** | **no trajectory at all**, 0 poses from the whole bag; buffer saturates at 301 samples / 3.000 s |
| `window_seconds = 1.0`, gate off | 0.990 s, 100 samples | 1.099 s | the requested window, delivered |
| `window_seconds = 1.0`, gate on (default) | 1.000 s, 101 samples, dispersion 23.06 deg | 5.099 s | gate ran to its timeout and said so: this rig never stops moving |

Honest caveat: on this sequence the gate's timeout landed on a window with *higher*
dispersion (23.06 deg) than the first one (2.58 deg), because the platform is in continuous
motion and the choice of window is then arbitrary. TIERS has no gravity-aligned survey
ground truth, so this cannot be scored as better or worse; the Oxford numbers above are
where the gate is actually measured.

Unit tests: `mola_imu_preintegration`, 18 cases, all pass.

---
Depends on MOLAorg/mola_imu_preintegration#14 (the `ImuInitialCalibrator` time window and
dispersion gate). Merge that first.

items.title: Journey Stage 1a: open a directory, on one path
items.body:
Framing: `docs/journey-stage1a-framing.md` (rev 8 — four review rounds,
two correction revisions found during implementation, one from review
round 1 of this PR).

`COHERENCE.md` §2 graded the golden product journey **broken at step 3**:

```
$ pmacs .
pmacs: Is a directory (os error 21)
EXIT=1
```

This fixes that arrow, on **one** path.

## What ships

- **The directory arm.** `resolve_target_buffer` answers a new
  `ResolvedTarget::Directory` *ahead* of the load — deliberately, since
  the EISDIR that killed startup came from `read_to_end` succeeding
  `File::open`.
- **The unification.** `EditorState::open` is rewritten as a caller of
  `resolve_target_buffer` rather than a parallel implementation of it, so
  the directory arm cannot be reached by one entry point and missed by
  another. The daemon/GPU bootstrap shares the same arm.
- **The resolver chain.** `path.open-directory` (short-circuit,
  first-claimant-wins) with `pmacs.path.directory_handler` as a
  replaceable fallback slot that dired fills. Deliberately *not* a dired
  hook subscription: `HookRegistry::add` only appends and builtins load
  before `init.lua`, so a subscribing builtin would always claim before
  any user listener could run.
- **The destination substrate.** The listing is async and the bootstrap
  is synchronous, so the whole post-await commit runs against a
  destination captured at request time (`pmacs.window.commit_to`).
- **`tests/journey_acceptance.rs`** — the first cross-subsystem
  acceptance suite (§19), **24 pins**, seeded with steps 2, 3, and 5. It
  is a ratchet: stages add rows, none removes them.

No protocol change — still v20.

## Notes for review

**The commit preflights before it invokes.** dired claims a handle,
captures `prev`, and paints long before it reaches anything that could
refuse, so validating at display time is four mutations too late and
leaves a hidden buffer behind. Every destination precondition — frontend
live, window live, buffer unchanged, window replaceable — is checked
before the callback runs at all.

**The scope pins the frontend, and only the frontend.** It swaps
`core.active_frontend` (not merely an override), because
`pmacs.window.buffer()`'s no-arg arm reads the ambient active buffer
directly. It does **not** pin the selected window — see round 1 below,
which is where that distinction turned out to matter.

**Awaiting inside a commit is refused.** A yield would restore the scope
while the coroutine is still parked, so the rest of the commit would
resume ambient.

**`replace_active_buffer` does not drop the startup scratch buffer**,
despite its doc comment having claimed so for as long as it has existed
— its body is one `switch_active_buffer` call. That comment misled the
framing through two revisions before anyone read the body. It is
corrected here because this PR would otherwise add more false references
to it; **changing the buffer lifetime is separate work.**

**Deliberate supersession.** The GPU initial-target framing's Q#GT6 and
acceptance 10 required a directory target to *fail* before window
creation. Directories now succeed; permission-denied and every other
pre-readiness failure keep that contract. Both documents are amended.

## Review round 1

**The captured window was not honored.** Framing §4.4 specified
`display{ window = dest:window() }`; the implementation still ended in
`pmacs.window.switch_buffer`, which targets whatever window the *scoped
frontend* has selected. A split or panel that took focus while
`read_dir` was pending therefore received the listing, and `prev` was
captured from it too — with every preflight check passing, because the
captured window was still live and still held its captured buffer.

Fixed at both sites; **N4c** added. Worth naming why 23 green pins
missed it: every routing pin varied *frontend* identity and none varied
the selected window within one frontend. Three pins on one axis read as
coverage of a two-axis space.

Two stale documentation claims found in the same round: the **§0
scorecard** still graded §2 "Broken at entry" while §2's own ground truth
had been rewritten (the scorecard is a second copy of the same claim, and
§19's row and ground truth were stale the same way — this PR creates the
suite §19 grades as missing); and **P4** still read "leaves exactly one
buffer", the exact claim rev 6 corrected as false everywhere else. The
test was already written correctly; only the framing lied.

## Bite results

Each mutation was run against the whole suite:

| mutation | fails |
|---|---|
| scope stops swapping `core.active_frontend` | N6a, P3 — nothing else |
| preflight moved after the callback | P1, P2 — nothing else |
| drop the `ScopedFrontend` arm from `acting_frontend` | N4b — nothing else |
| dired's `display` back to `switch_buffer` | N4c — nothing else |
| `prev` read from the ambient window | N4c — nothing else |

The third is why **N4b** exists: it left N4 green, because
`ScopedFrontend::enter`'s ambient swap answers correctly on its own. The
override is load-bearing in exactly one case — a commit reached from
inside an interactive command — and nothing pinned it until the mutation
said so. The last two are round 1's, and each falsifies N4c
independently.

Two pins were removed or relabelled rather than weakened: **P7 is gone**
(Q#JR12 is structural — `run` computes `had_file = file.is_some()`, so
there is no directory-specific branch to break), and **P1/P2 are noted
as also failing on full revert**, since `commit_to` does not exist on
the pre-image.

## Folded in: PR #180 (docs-only)

Two open documentation PRs editing the same three ledger files
re-conflict on every merge to `main` — the treadmill #169 and #176 each
paid three resolution rounds for. #180 was docs-only and already
CONFLICTING; it is folded here so one writer owns those files. **#180
should be closed, not merged.** What it carried:

- Handoff §1's terminal configuration + copy mode arc bullet (#173,
  #178) and the GPU-terminal-input landed docs (#168).
- Handoff §4's `Buffer::set_generated_contents` substrate invariant —
  the one authorized write for a generated buffer, with the three
  non-obvious properties four review rounds found (an intercept is not
  read-only; a bare `set_read_only` refuses the owner's own refresh; a
  rope write is only half an edit).
- COHERENCE §14's record that **four writer mechanisms have not adopted
  it** and remain emptiable by `M-x buffer.undo`.
- The active-work lane removals for the merged terminal arcs.

This branch also integrates `githubsucks/main` @ `42025e4` (Lean 4 Stage
4b #181) by merge rather than rebase, since it is under review.

Three claims were corrected rather than picked while resolving:

- **The head-of-`main` anchor.** Both sides named `74301d1`, no longer
  true. Now `42025e4`, and the active-work **recovery floor moved with
  it** — that section's own rule is that a floor accepting an older
  commit than the declared base passes on a tree the file does not
  describe.
- **The Lean 4 bullet contradicted the anchor.** Header still said
  "stages 1, 2, 3a, 3b LANDED" and Stage 4b still said "in review".
  Both corrected.
- **The COHERENCE §2 grade.** #180 still carried "broken at step 3" in
  the ground truth *and* the §0 scorecard; this PR's corrections win,
  since the code change here is what makes them true.

## Gates

`cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D
warnings`; `cargo test --lib` (1849); `--lib --features crdt` (2033);
**journey 24**, dired 25, find_file 8 (unmodified), bottom_panel_stage1
46, gpu_initial_target 1; `m4_acceptance --skip basedpyright` (121);
`PMACS_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo test -p pmacs-gpu` (202); `cargo test
--workspace --skip basedpyright` clean; `git diff --check`. Re-run in
full after folding in #180 and `42025e4`, including `lean_input` (31)
and `auto_pair` (45), which #181 touches.

One note on the workspace sweep: 11 `compile_mode_acceptance` failures
turned out to be **environmental, not code** — a personal
`~/.config/pmacs/init.lua` defines `find-file`, which #162 now ships, so
`command.define` refuses to overwrite. Green with a clean `HOME`.
(COHERENCE §19 already records that this suite reads the real user
config, as an unintentional whole-product test.)

items.title: Session 3 (Sprint 2): TLS + DNS checks + Sprint 1 corrections
items.body:
## Summary

Sprint 2 (TLS + DNS) per `CLAUDE.md` §9, plus the 3 Sprint 1 audit observations.

### Sprint 1 corrections

1. **HSTS-in-JSON** — verified ground truth (`cat results/s1_headers_telemo.json` from the local file kept by `.gitignore`): the finding IS in the JSON, console summary matches exactly. **Not a bug.** Added the regression test `test_hsts_completely_missing_yields_high_finding` anyway.
2. **CHAIN_DEPENDENCY auto-tagger** — `_apply_chain_dependency()` runs after `evaluate_headers()` and tags every finding sharing an `evidence[0]` string with `≥ 2` peers. Real example: a CSP value containing both `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` produces 2 findings; both now carry `CHAIN_DEPENDENCY`. Negative test confirms unrelated findings don't get the flag.
3. **Imperva/Incapsula signature** — new check matching `ipmsperf_uuid` in `Set-Cookie` → `INFO` + `CONTEXT_DEPENDENT` (Sprint 3 phishing surface needs the WAF context). The `HEADERS_CHECKS` dict format gained an optional `flags` field, propagated into `Finding.flags`.

### Sprint 2 — TLS (`tools/_tls.py`)

- subprocess wrapper around `testssl.sh -p -S -f -h` (protocols + server defaults / cert / FS / headers).
- Line parser: SSLv2/SSLv3 → CRITICAL, TLS1.0/1.1 → HIGH, TLS1.2 → LOW (acceptable), FS absent → HIGH.
- Cert-expiration helper handles **four** testssl shapes including the tricky `expires < 30 days (29) (date --> date)` form (regression test).
- HSTS recognised under both `HSTS` and `Strict Transport Security` labels; `not offered` → HIGH, `offered` without `preload` → LOW.
- `evidence` = exact testssl line stripped.

### Sprint 2 — DNS (`tools/_dns.py`)

- `dig +short` for DNSKEY / TXT / MX.

items.title: Add multi-frequency waveform inversion script with virtual-element sparse-array support
items.body:
### Motivation
- Provide a standalone MATLAB implementation of multi-frequency waveform inversion for ultrasound tomography with support for sparse-array enhancement via virtual elements.
- Enable joint sound-speed (SoS) and attenuation inversion with a segmented frequency schedule and per-frequency iteration control.
- Add visualization and reproducibility features including per-iteration GIF export and optional ground-truth ingestion from a GIF. 
- Support practical preprocessing like phase-screen correction, illumination compensation, ringing-removal filtering, and outlier channel masking. 

### Description
- Add new script `FuWs/MultiFrequencyWaveformInvKCI_fws20260415.m` implementing DTFT-based frequency extraction, Helmholtz forward/adjoint solves (via `HelmholtzSolver`), and a nonlinear conjugate-gradient inversion loop for SoS and attenuation. 
- Implement virtual-element augmentation with `unilateral` and `bilateral` modes and interpolation kernels (`zoh`/`linear`), including mapping of discretized TOFs and confidence weighting for virtual receivers. 
- Include preprocessing and robustness features: phase-screen correction, per-frequency outlier removal, illumination preconditioning, ringing-removal filter (`ringingRemovalFilt`), and configurable near-end exclusion. 
- Add visualization, outputs, and helpers: iterative 2x2 display, per-iteration GIF export (`gif_filepath`), ground-truth reading from GIF via `readTruthFromGif` and `indexedToVelocity`, saving of results to `*_WaveformInversionResults.mat`, and small utility `ternary`. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were added or executed for this change.
